repos/laceyenterprises/agent-os/pulls/81.body:
## Summary

Thread an explicit unattended mode through the real installer entry points, with early missing-input and prompt refusal, Colima provisioning, and strict post-provision readiness before runtime service installation. Preserve attended choices and make unsupported OAuth/Keychain and protected GUI coverage visible.



## What changed

bootstrap/install-agent-os.sh, bootstrap/bootstrap.sh, bootstrap/install.sh and scripts/install-agent-os-runtime.sh consume the shared bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh boundary. It closes stdin, forces no-prompt sudo/Git behavior, requires explicit lab Git identity and Keychain exclusion, confines the password argv exception to an acknowledged disposable guest, and rejects unsupported migration credential/GUI/model phases before selector persistence. Dependencies precede clone/GnuPG/CFG loading; both canonical bundle call sites use the same Colima/CLI-only lab selection and fail on partial provisioning. Post-provision checklist JSON is classified by TIH-01 under a subprocess-group deadline before runtime/duplicate-PgBouncer service mutation. Combined migration preflight defers pooled readiness until the existing provisioning/readiness path. Existing wrapper and preflight fixtures gain scoped regression cases. modules/test-install-host/README.md contains the reached-branch disposition table and evidence limitations.


## Why it matters

Fresh lab attempts must surface missing inputs, hidden prompts and partial dependency installs early, without routine operator recovery. Proposal: use Colima for the lab core path and withhold qualification until its pinned nested combination is proved. OAuth/browser consent, production Keychain recovery, protected GUI/LuLu/TCC/Touch ID consent, private overlays, paid model routing and production notification/credential coverage remain named exclusions; a required exclusion never counts green. No new CI check, workflow, manifest, ratchet or override is proposed or added.


## Post-merge activities

Lab-only: after TIH-04 credential profiles, TIH-05 controller tooling and TIH-08 hardware-specific authorization are available, provision the dedicated lab, use trusted root/restart runbooks, and collect real readiness, doctor, five-lane smoke and cold-reboot health evidence. Prove Colima nesting before qualification. No production host deployment/restart is part of this PR; implementation is not live or qualified from fixtures.

## Ticket
TIH-02

## Spec
test-install-host@655efb6fd9dc

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
high

## Acceptance evidence

Managed exact-head push: local CI mirror budget-deferred after two budget overruns; GitHub CI and AMA still gate merge. Bounded local validation: wrapper 31 assertions pass; TIH-01 contracts/checks 53 tests pass; bootstrap UID, Claude OAuth, KB and OpenClaw decommission contracts pass; full bootstrap/install.orchestrator.test.sh passes within its 900-second bound (the initial 120-second attempt timed out); sync-validation, synthetic smoke and OMB fixtures pass. Runtime Keychain preflight and os-startup prune, deploy-guard, promoted-daemon auth, orphan-reaper installer and AGY recovery slices pass. Bash syntax, git diff --check and the existing ShellCheck baseline gate pass.

Existing red fixture evidence is preserved, not counted as passing: preflight 10/11 (including the new pooled-ordering case) and PgBouncer 13/14; their happy-path regex-log and stale-socket assertions respectively reproduce on origin/main. The existing runtime Node suite has the same 13 failing test names on origin/main and this change under isolated account-home lookup (8 pass / 21 total). Its initial ordinary run attempted a native Keychain settings operation which macOS denied; subsequent baseline/current runs used disposable scratch homes. No unrelated baseline fix, new guard or test bypass is included. No concurrency fix was made. Real lab install, nesting, reboot, GUI/FileVault and OAuth/production auth evidence is unavailable, not passing. Alert/pager sends in the scoped installer fixtures are mocked; no full worker-pool, main-catchup, sentinel or PMV suite was run.

## Out-of-scope changes

(none)

 ---
 
+## Installer contracts and recovery
+
+`--non-interactive` / `AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` now selects the unattended
+lab profile throughout the wrapper, bootstrap and runtime installer; it no
+longer merely skips wizard prompts. Supply `AGENT_OS_MODE=dual|single`,
+`AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME`, `AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL`, and
+`AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1`. Explicit Git identity satisfies
+readiness without writing global Git configuration. Selecting an agent workspace
+also requires a lab `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`; core-only readiness explicitly
+excludes workspace authentication. The token is unset after validation and
+supplied only to the readiness authentication probe.
+
+This profile uses Colima and Docker CLI/Compose, excludes the 1Password GUI and
+protected desktop casks, and skips Keychain bridge installation, OAuth broker
+health and Touch ID. These exclusions do not qualify live OAuth or GUI coverage.
+Creating a disposable guest account also requires the password/argv exception
+acknowledgements documented in `modules/test-install-host/README.md`.
+
+Sudo must authorize operations noninteractively. Executing privileged children
+requires SETENV (or an ALL policy) for the explicit preserved environment;
+list, validate and query probes omit environment preservation.
+
+Bootstrap disables the duplicate Homebrew PgBouncer service before readiness.
+The first successful readiness gate records
+`.agent-os/install-state/readiness-v1` under the install checkout before runtime
+mutation. A rerun honors that checkpoint and reaches runtime, plist, compose
+and health repair even with Agent OS ports occupied. Remove the checkpoint to
+request a new clean-host readiness assessment. It records installer progress,
+not current health or a qualified lab acceptance result.
+
+Attended installs also have visible changes: wrapper Homebrew bundles always
+provision core dependencies and any bundle failure is fatal; combined
+`install.sh --preflight --phase-1-apps` provisions apps before preflight
+(standalone preflight remains read-only); bootstrap refuses non-TTY stdin unless
+unattended mode is explicit. Runtime installation now follows service-account,
+broker-secret and Keychain bridge setup at section 5.9.
+
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared, opt-in prompt refusal for the reached installer chain.
+installer_unattended_init() {
+  case "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" in
+    0) return 0 ;;
+    1) ;;
+    *) printf 'unattended-input: AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE must be 0 or 1\n' >&2; return 64 ;;
+  esac
+  set +x +v
+  export AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 CI=1 GH_ASSUME_YES=1
+  export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  export SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  # Ignore a supplied interactive SSH command: unattended cannot inherit an agent
+  # or password prompt. Host verification remains enabled.
+  export GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oIdentityAgent=none -oBatchMode=yes -oConnectTimeout=15 -oServerAliveInterval=15 -oServerAliveCountMax=3'
+  export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1
+  exec </dev/null
+}
+
+installer_unattended_sudo_check() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  [[ "$(id -u)" == 0 ]] && return 0
+  command sudo -n true || {
+    printf 'unattended-input: pre-authorized noninteractive sudo required\n' >&2
+    return 77
+  }
+}
+
+# Functions preserve attended argv exactly. Export only in unattended mode so
+# reached Bash helpers also refuse askpass. sudo policies still authorize every
+# operation; a cached timestamp is never treated as an enduring grant.
+installer_unattended_functions() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  sudo() {
+    local arg query=0 args=()
+    for arg in "$@"; do
+      case "$arg" in -l|-ll|--list|-v|--validate|-V|--version|-h|--help|-k|-K) query=1 ;; esac
+      [[ "$arg" == -A ]] || args+=("$arg")
+    done
+    if [[ "$query" == 1 ]]; then
+      command sudo -n "${args[@]}"
+      return
+    fi
+    command sudo -n --preserve-env=AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE,GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT,GIT_ASKPASS,SSH_ASKPASS,GIT_SSH_COMMAND,GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME,GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL,GIT_COMMITTER_NAME,GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL,SUDO_ASKPASS "${args[@]}"
+  }
+  git() {
+    local identity=()
+    if [[ -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" && -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+      identity=(-c "user.name=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" -c "user.email=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL")
+    fi
+    command git "${identity[@]}" -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=/usr/bin/false \
+      -c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0 -c fetch.writeCommitGraph=false "$@"
+  }
+  export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'credential.helper=' 'core.askPass=/usr/bin/false' 'maintenance.auto=false' 'gc.auto=0' 'fetch.writeCommitGraph=false'"
+  export -f sudo git
+}
+
+installer_unattended_core_inputs() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: acknowledge unsupported OAuth/Keychain with AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  if [[ -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: explicit AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME and AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL required\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME"
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL"
+}
+
+# Only idempotent provisioning operations belong here. Unknown and structural
+# failures stop immediately; a transient signature never overrides an auth,
+# permission, certificate-verification or configuration error in the same run.
+installer_output_is_transient() {
+  local kind="$1" diagnostic_tail
+  shift
+  diagnostic_tail="$(tail -n 20 "$@")"
+  if grep -Eiq 'permission denied|operation not permitted|authentication failed|could not read (username|password)|repository .*not found|repository not found|host key verification failed|certificate verify failed|certificate verification failed|unable to get local issuer certificate|self.signed certificate|invalid (argument|configuration|plist)|no such file or directory|EACCES|EPERM|E401|E403' <<<"$diagnostic_tail"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$kind" == runtime ]] && grep -Eiq 'bootstrap failed: 5: input/output error|(^|[^[:alnum:]_])EIO([^[:alnum:]_]|$)|resource temporarily unavailable|service not yet bootstrapped' <<<"$diagnostic_tail"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  grep -Eiq 'timed out|timeout|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|EAI_AGAIN|connection reset|connection refused|temporary failure in name resolution|could not resolve host|could not resolve hostname|TLS handshake|SSL.*(connect|handshake)|early EOF|remote end hung up unexpectedly|HTTP[^[:digit:]]+50[234]|(error|response|returned)[^[:digit:]]+50[234]' <<<"$diagnostic_tail"
+}
+
+installer_run_with_retry() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  local capture_dir attempt status delay
+  capture_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return 1
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    status=0
+    "$@" >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" || status=$?
+    cat "$capture_dir/stdout"
+    cat "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2
+    if [[ "$status" == 0 ]]; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! installer_output_is_transient "$kind" "$capture_dir/stderr"; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return "$status"
+    fi
+    # Fixed provisioning policy, matching the launchd post-bootout recovery
+    # window. No exponential arithmetic or retry tuning inputs to duplicate.
+    case "$attempt" in 1) delay=2 ;; 2) delay=5 ;; esac
+    printf 'unattended-retry: %s transient failure on attempt %s/3; retrying in %ss\n' "$kind" "$attempt" "$delay" >&2
+    sleep "$delay"
+  done
+}
+
+# Existing producer + TIH-01 strict adapter, before launchd mutations. No auth
+# probe is executed on the builder host; callers run this only in the lab install.
+installer_unattended_precheck() {
+  local repo_root="$1" stage="$2" timeout_seconds="${3:-120}"
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0

+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile

+try:

+except ValueError:

+from checks import adapt
+from contracts import Stage
+
+

+    if diagnostics:

+            mode="w", prefix="agent-os-precheck-", suffix=".stderr", delete=False
+        ) as diagnostic_file:
+            diagnostic_file.write(diagnostics)

+
+
+process = subprocess.Popen(
+    ["bash", str(root / "scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh"), "--json"],
+    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, start_new_session=True,
+)

+    raw, diagnostics = process.communicate(timeout=timeout_seconds)
+except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

+# Core-only installs explicitly exclude workspace authentication.

+    if not baseline.qualified:
+        raise ValueError

+# forwarded into the installer log. Actual boot provenance belongs to TIH-05.

+PYCODE
+}
+
+installer_brew_bundle() {
+  local brew_bin="$1" brewfile="$2" temporary_file status
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$brewfile" --no-lock
+    return
+  fi
+  temporary_file="$(mktemp)" || return 1
+  # Preserve the canonical formula inventory and CLI casks only.
+  awk '$1 != "cask" || $2 == "\"1password-cli\"" || $2 == "\"claude-code\"" || $2 == "\"codex\"" { print }' \
+    "$brewfile" >"$temporary_file" || { rm -f "$temporary_file"; return 1; }
+  printf 'brew "colima"\nbrew "docker"\nbrew "docker-compose"\n' >>"$temporary_file"
+  status=0
+  installer_run_with_retry network "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$temporary_file" --no-lock || status=$?
+  rm -f "$temporary_file"
+  [[ "$status" == 0 ]] || {
+    printf 'dependency provisioning failed; refusing partial install\n' >&2
+    return "$status"
+  }
+  printf 'coverage-excluded: protected GUI casks (LuLu/TCC, Docker Desktop, desktop applications)\n' >&2
+}
+
+
+# Only a passed initial gate creates this install-root checkpoint. Subsequent
+# runs resume idempotent runtime steps even when our services hold the ports.
+installer_unattended_readiness() {
+  local repo_root="$1" marker="$1/.agent-os/install-state/readiness-v1" owner="${2:-}"
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  if [[ -f "$marker" ]] && [[ "$(cat "$marker")" == readiness-v1 ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-recovery: readiness checkpoint accepted; resuming runtime installation\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  AGENT_NAME="${AGENT_NAME:-}" OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="${INSTALLER_OP_TOKEN:-}" installer_unattended_precheck "$repo_root" readiness || return
+  if [[ -n "$owner" ]]; then
+    sudo -u "$owner" mkdir -p "$(dirname "$marker")" || return
+    printf 'readiness-v1\n' | sudo -u "$owner" tee "$marker" >/dev/null || return
+  else
+    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$marker")" || return
+    printf 'readiness-v1\n' >"$marker" || return
+  fi
+}

Explicit install identity satisfies Git readiness; core-only installs explicitly exclude workspace authentication. A passed gate writes `.agent-os/install-state/readiness-v1` before runtime mutation; reruns honor the checkpoint to resume with services already holding ports. Homebrew PgBouncer reconciliation precedes the gate. This checkpoint is progress, not current-health acceptance. Warnings, malformed JSON, interactive sudo or missing checks refuse. Only normalized check-ID reasons enter the installer log. On failure or timeout, nonempty stderr is preserved in a mode-0600 `agent-os-precheck-*.stderr` temporary file and its path is logged; the invoking operator should inspect and remove it after diagnosis. Successful prechecks leave no diagnostic file. The clean initial baseline inventory belongs to TIH-05's controller before invoking the installer. |

Owner/domain and fail-before-bootout validation belong to TIH-03. This PR neither bounces production services nor certifies every registry service's live health. |

HTTP health retries have connection/request bounds; both retry loops advance without `set -e` exiting on a zero post-increment. Optional OpenClaw is probed only when enabled; OAuth/Keychain checks stay excluded in unattended mode. |

Attended behavior remains available; unattended migration OMB/Open WebUI selection refuses before persistence, and future test profiles must constrain endpoints/credentials and name coverage. No Tailscale replacement or distributed dispatch work is included. |
+

+reboot evidence. Root/restart actions follow trusted runbooks and TIH-08's
+hardware-specific authorization. Fixture success proves refusal and ordering
+contracts; it does not prove macOS/Colima nesting, GUI/FileVault readiness,
+production credentials, or a live install. No deployment or real lab evidence
+was collected while authoring TIH-02.

+TIH-02 scoped acceptance evidence: wrapper fixtures pass 31 assertions, including
+closed stdin, direct-entry input refusal, guest-password redaction, shared
+attended/unattended dependency selection, strict readiness classification and a

+OMB, runtime Keychain/preflight/prune, deploy-guard, promoted-auth, orphan-reaper

+120-second bound expired; the scoped rerun uses a 900-second bound.

+assertion and PgBouncer's stale-socket cleanup assertion both reproduce on
+`origin/main`. The runtime Node suite reports the same 13 failing test names
+(8 passing / 21 total) on `origin/main` and this change when account-home lookup
+is isolated to disposable scratch state. Its first ordinary run attempted a
+native Keychain settings call and macOS denied interaction; subsequent baseline

+or real-machine evidence. Existing fixture repairs outside this slice are not
+included. ShellCheck's existing baseline gate and Bash syntax checks are used;
+no new CI check, gate, ratchet, manifest entry or override is proposed.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared, opt-in prompt refusal for the reached installer chain.
+installer_unattended_init() {
+  case "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" in
+    0) return 0 ;;
+    1) ;;
+    *) printf 'unattended-input: AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE must be 0 or 1\n' >&2; return 64 ;;
+  esac
+  set +x +v
+  export AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 CI=1 GH_ASSUME_YES=1
+  export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  export SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  # Ignore a supplied interactive SSH command: unattended cannot inherit an agent
+  # or password prompt. Host verification remains enabled.
+  export GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oIdentityAgent=none -oBatchMode=yes -oConnectTimeout=15 -oServerAliveInterval=15 -oServerAliveCountMax=3'
+  export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1
+  exec </dev/null
+}
+
+installer_unattended_sudo_check() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  [[ "$(id -u)" == 0 ]] && return 0
+  command sudo -n true || {
+    printf 'unattended-input: pre-authorized noninteractive sudo required\n' >&2
+    return 77
+  }
+}
+
+# Functions preserve attended argv exactly. Export only in unattended mode so
+# reached Bash helpers also refuse askpass. sudo policies still authorize every
+# operation; a cached timestamp is never treated as an enduring grant.
+installer_unattended_functions() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  sudo() {
+    local arg args=()
+    for arg in "$@"; do
+      [[ "$arg" == -A ]] || args+=("$arg")
+    done
+    command sudo -n --preserve-env=AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE,GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT,GIT_ASKPASS,SSH_ASKPASS,GIT_SSH_COMMAND,GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME,GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL,GIT_COMMITTER_NAME,GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL,SUDO_ASKPASS "${args[@]}"
+  }
+  git() {
+    local identity=()
+    if [[ -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" && -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+      identity=(-c "user.name=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" -c "user.email=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL")
+    fi
+    command git "${identity[@]}" -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=/usr/bin/false \
+      -c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0 -c fetch.writeCommitGraph=false "$@"
+  }
+  export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'credential.helper=' 'core.askPass=/usr/bin/false' 'maintenance.auto=false' 'gc.auto=0' 'fetch.writeCommitGraph=false'"
+  export -f sudo git
+}
+
+installer_unattended_core_inputs() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: acknowledge unsupported OAuth/Keychain with AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  if [[ -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: explicit AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME and AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL required\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME"
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL"
+}
+
+# Only idempotent provisioning operations belong here. Unknown and structural
+# failures stop immediately; a transient signature never overrides an auth,
+# permission, certificate-verification or configuration error in the same run.
+installer_output_is_transient() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if grep -Eiq 'permission denied|operation not permitted|authentication failed|could not read (username|password)|repository .*not found|repository not found|host key verification failed|certificate verify failed|certificate verification failed|unable to get local issuer certificate|self.signed certificate|invalid (argument|configuration|plist)|no such file or directory|EACCES|EPERM|E401|E403' "$@"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$kind" == runtime ]] && grep -Eiq 'bootstrap failed: 5: input/output error|(^|[^[:alnum:]_])EIO([^[:alnum:]_]|$)|resource temporarily unavailable|service not yet bootstrapped' "$@"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  grep -Eiq 'timed out|timeout|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|EAI_AGAIN|connection reset|connection refused|temporary failure in name resolution|could not resolve host|could not resolve hostname|TLS handshake|SSL.*(connect|handshake)|early EOF|remote end hung up unexpectedly|HTTP[^[:digit:]]+50[234]|(error|response|returned)[^[:digit:]]+50[234]' "$@"
+}
+
+installer_run_with_retry() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  local capture_dir attempt status delay
+  capture_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return 1
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    status=0
+    "$@" >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" || status=$?
+    cat "$capture_dir/stdout"
+    cat "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2
+    if [[ "$status" == 0 ]]; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! installer_output_is_transient "$kind" "$capture_dir/stdout" "$capture_dir/stderr"; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return "$status"
+    fi
+    # Fixed provisioning policy, matching the launchd post-bootout recovery
+    # window. No exponential arithmetic or retry tuning inputs to duplicate.
+    case "$attempt" in 1) delay=2 ;; 2) delay=5 ;; esac
+    printf 'unattended-retry: %s transient failure on attempt %s/3; retrying in %ss\n' "$kind" "$attempt" "$delay" >&2
+    sleep "$delay"
+  done
+}
+
+# Existing producer + TIH-01 strict adapter, before launchd mutations. No auth
+# probe is executed on the builder host; callers run this only in the lab install.
+installer_unattended_precheck() {
+  local repo_root="$1" stage="$2" timeout_seconds="${3:-120}"
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  python3 - "$repo_root" "$stage" "$timeout_seconds" <<'PYCODE'
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+stage = sys.argv[2]
+try:
+    timeout_seconds = float(sys.argv[3])
+    if not 0 < timeout_seconds <= 120:
+        raise ValueError
+except ValueError:

repos/laceyenterprises/agent-os/pulls/81.body:
## Adversarial Review — Gemini (gemini-reviewer-lacey)

> Reviewer: gemini · Gemini 3.1 Pro (High) · none

## Summary
The PR implements an explicit unattended mode across the installation and migration scripts, substituting interactive prompts with strict requirements for environment inputs. It intercepts `sudo` and `git` commands to guarantee non-interactive execution and properly enforces `AGENT_OS_DISPOSABLE_GUEST` during password handling. However, the implementation introduces a blocking operational violation by converting several transient subprocess errors (such as those from `git clone` and `launchctl bootstrap` via `os-restart.sh`) into immediate fatal installation failures in unattended mode.

## Blocking issues
- **Transient subprocess errors treated as fatal**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/bootstrap.sh`
  - **Lines:** 594-600, 1205-1213
  - **Problem:** The diff introduces immediate, terminal `fail` calls for system commands when `AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`. Specifically, if `sudo "$AGENT_OS_ROOT/scripts/os-restart.sh" --install-only` (which invokes `launchctl bootstrap`) fails, the script evaluates the `else` block and executes `fail "runtime plist installation failed"` (line 1209). Similarly, if `git clone "$repo" "$dest"` fails, it executes `fail "requested repository clone failed"` (line 596). This same fatal pattern without retry is applied to `npm install` (line 512), `colima start` (line 1088), and `brew bundle` (in `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`). I confirmed there is no surrounding retry block for any of these commands.
  - **Why it matters:** macOS launchd routinely returns transient errors like `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` (EIO) if a prior bootout hasn't settled. Similarly, `git clone` and package managers (`npm`, `brew`) frequently fail due to transient network timeouts or TLS handshake failures. Terminating the entire unattended installer upon the first occurrence of these common transient errors turns them into permanent lab provision outages, explicitly violating the operational behavior rule for subprocess transient errors.
  - **Recommended fix:** Classify transient errors from these subprocesses (e.g., EIO for launchd, network/timeout/TLS errors for `git` and package managers) and retry with bounded backoff rather than immediately calling `fail`. Retain immediate escalation for non-transient errors.

## Non-blocking issues
- **Precheck subprocess stderr swallowed**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`
  - **Lines:** 101-102
  - **Problem:** In `installer_unattended_precheck`, the `subprocess.Popen` call sets `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL`.
  - **Why it matters:** If `scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh` fails due to an unexpected syntax error, missing dependency, or crash, all diagnostic output is swallowed. This obscures the root cause and makes it harder for an operator to debug why the precheck failed or timed out.
  - **Recommended fix:** Capture stderr (`subprocess.PIPE`) and include it in the timeout/error message, or log it to a designated debug file (ensuring any secrets are still sanitized if needed).

## Suggested fixes
1. Implement a `retry_with_backoff` wrapper in `unattended.sh` or `bootstrap.sh` that checks the exit code and/or stderr of `os-restart.sh`, `git clone`, and the package manager commands.
2. Wrap the failing calls in `bootstrap.sh` with this retry logic before escalating to `fail` in unattended mode.
3. In `installer_unattended_precheck`, change `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` to `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` and safely log or output the errors upon failure.

## Verdict
Request changes

## Adversarial Review — Gemini (gemini-reviewer-lacey)

> Reviewer: gemini · Gemini 3.1 Pro (High) · none

## Summary

I reviewed the unattended installer implementation, focusing on the load-bearing operational constraints, cross-user boundary safety, and failure recovery. The PR cleanly implements unattended mode with robust guards: it correctly isolates the `sysadminctl` argv password exception to disposable guests, enforces pre-authorized `sudo` without falling back to a terminal prompt, properly restricts Keychain/OAuth interactions, and delegates system calls to a well-classified subprocess retry helper that respects transient EIO and network errors. It explicitly handles the `git clone` partial-failure state by splitting submodule initialization so transient failures can be recovered without discarding the parent checkout. The implementation is solid.

## Blocking issues

- None.

## Non-blocking issues

- **Divergent clone logic between modes**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/install-agent-os.sh`
  - **Lines:** 763-775
  - **Problem:** The unattended branch separates `git clone` and `git submodule update` into two independent steps to preserve a populated parent checkout upon submodule transfer failure, but the attended branch still uses a single `git clone --recurse-submodules`.
  - **Why it matters:** While attended mode does not use automatic retries, an operator manually rerunning the script after a submodule network timeout will encounter a "destination path already exists" error because the parent clone is left behind, forcing them to manually delete it before retrying. Keeping both paths identical reduces operator friction and maintenance divergence.
  - **Recommended fix:** Unify the logic by using the split `git clone` and `git submodule update --init --recursive` operations for both attended and unattended modes, removing `--recurse-submodules` entirely.

## Suggested fixes

- Apply the single non-blocking recommendation to unify the `git clone` and `submodule update` steps across both attended and unattended modes.

## Verdict

Comment only

## Adversarial Review — Claude (claude-reviewer-lacey)

> Reviewer: claude · claude-opus-5-5 · high

## Summary
The unattended installer path has a recovery gap. The new strict readiness gate runs `pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh` through the TIH-01 adapter at `Stage.READINESS`, where any non-pass check makes the install unqualified. That gate sits before runtime/launchd mutation in every unattended `bootstrap.sh` run. Two things it checks are things the installer itself creates or deliberately leaves unset:
- **Ports:** the Colima-forwarded compose ports (4000, 3001, 3100, 3200, 4317, 9092). In-use ports are reported as `warn`.
- **Global Git identity:** the installer never writes one; it only sets env and `-c` identity.

So an unattended install that fails after the runtime step cannot be resumed by re-running it. The PR now makes those later failures fatal: os-restart, compose start, and the health budget. This is the partial-failure-not-recoverable / preflight-refuses-recovery pattern.

Other findings are advisory:
- the existing `--non-interactive` contract changed under scripted callers;
- the precheck runs on `python3` from PATH instead of the provisioned interpreter;
- the service-account token stays exported for the rest of the run;
- retry classification scans the whole output;
- some behavior changed for attended runs.

I did not find secret leakage to a public surface, a migration, or a mapped-SPEC trigger. The changed paths are not in the spec-mapping table.

## Blocking issues
- **Readiness gate blocks rerun after partial unattended install**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/bootstrap.sh`, `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`
  - **Lines:** `bootstrap.sh` 5.9 block (`installer_unattended_precheck "$AGENT_OS_ROOT" readiness \|\| fail ...`), `check_health` / `start_stack` / os-restart unattended `fail` branches; `unattended.sh` `installer_unattended_precheck`
  - **Problem:** Every unattended `bootstrap.sh` run calls `installer_unattended_precheck ... readiness` before the runtime installer. That runs `scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh --json` through `checks.adapt(stage=READINESS)`, which adds a reason for every non-`pass` check (`checks.py` ~L119).
    - **Ports:** the checklist records `port-<n>` as `warn` whenever `lsof` sees a listener. Section 7 then starts the compose stacks under the admin user's Colima, so the forwarded ports (LiteLLM 4000, Grafana 3001, Loki 3100, Tempo 3200, OTLP 4317, Prometheus 9092) are visible to the admin's `lsof`.
    - **Fatal steps after the gate:** this PR makes these unattended failures fatal: `sudo os-restart.sh --install-only`, `start_stack`, `start_agent_control_stack`, and `check_health` (for example, LiteLLM missing `auth` within 18×5s, or Agent Control).
    - **What happens:** once a run gets past section 7 and then fails, every rerun stops at readiness with `warn:port-4000` and similar. It never reaches the idempotent runtime, plist, compose, or health steps again. A fully successful unattended install also cannot be re-run.
    - **Git identity:** the checklist's `git-config` check reads `git config --global user.name/user.email`. The installer supplies identity only through `GIT_AUTHOR_*` env and `-c user.name=` (which `--global` reads ignore) and never writes global config. On a truly fresh lab host the gate therefore fails on the first run as well, unless the lab pre-seeds `~/.gitconfig`. That makes `AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME/EMAIL` redundant.
    - **Token:** the same applies to `op-cli-auth` when no `AGENT_NAME` is selected, because nothing requires or exports a token in that case.
  - **Why it matters:** This is the load-bearing "partial-failure state not recoverable" / "preflight refuses recovery instead of attempting it" pattern. The step-1 state (services started) permanently blocks step 2 (finishing or repairing the install). The operator then has to tear down services, or hand-run the remaining steps, before the installer can proceed. That is the routine recovery the PR says it removes. The guard knows the conflicting holders are its own services and knows the missing global identity value, yet it refuses.
  - **Recommended fix:** Make the readiness stage re-entrant. Either:
    - run the readiness gate only when no prior-attempt marker or install state exists, and record a durable "readiness passed for this attempt" marker that later reruns honor; or
    - pass the expected Agent OS listeners (canonical labels and compose projects) to the adapter as an allowlist of self-owned holders, so only foreign holders count.

    Also, in unattended mode, write `git config --global user.name/email` from `AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME/EMAIL` for the invoking user before the precheck, or make the adapter accept the explicit install identity. Either require `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` unconditionally in unattended core inputs, or exclude `op-cli-auth` explicitly when no workspace is selected. Add a fixture: a rerun with the canonical ports held must reach the runtime installer.

## Non-blocking issues
- **Existing `--non-interactive` scripted contract silently repurposed**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/install-agent-os.sh`
  - **Lines:** usage text, `main()`, `install_harnesses()`, `hand_off_to_bootstrap` env export
  - **Problem:** `bootstrap/AGENTS.md` documents `AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` + `AGENT_OS_MODE` for scripted green-field installs. That flag now:
    - requires lab-only inputs (`AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1`, Git name/email);
    - exports unattended mode into `bootstrap.sh`;
    - swaps Docker Desktop for Colima;
    - drops the 1Password GUI cask;
    - skips the keychain bridge, OAuth broker health checks, and Touch ID.
  - **Why it matters:** Existing scripted callers either start refusing, or (once they add the acknowledgement) get a lab-profile install with OAuth/Keychain excluded. AGENTS.md was not updated to say so.
  - **Recommended fix:** Update `bootstrap/AGENTS.md` (and the fresh-Mac runbook) to describe the new unattended contract and its exclusions. Alternatively, keep a separate selector for the old "skip wrapper prompts only" behavior.
- **Readiness adapter runs on PATH `python3`, not provisioned interpreter**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`
  - **Lines:** `installer_unattended_precheck` (`python3 - ...`)
  - **Problem:** `contracts.py` uses `enum.StrEnum` and `X | None`, which need Python 3.11 or later. Bootstrap provisions `python@3.14` and exports `HQ_PYTHON3`, but the precheck invokes whatever `python3` resolves to. That may be Apple's 3.9 CLT stub on a fresh host.
  - **Why it matters:** The adapter would fail with an ImportError traceback on stderr, outside `preserve_stderr`. The result would read as "readiness failed" rather than as an interpreter problem.
  - **Recommended fix:** Use `"${HQ_PYTHON3:-python3}"` and fail with a clear message if the interpreter version is below 3.11.
- **Service-account token stays exported for the rest of the unattended run**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/bootstrap.sh`
  - **Lines:** 5/8 validation block (`if [[ ... != 1 ]]; then unset OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN; fi`)
  - **Problem:** In unattended mode the token read from `op-service-account.env` is never unset. It is inherited by:
    - npm and brew children;
    - the runtime installer and the capture files of its retries;
    - compose `up` (a bare `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` passthrough in a compose file would inject it into containers);
    - every process `ps eww` can see.
  - **Why it matters:** This widens credential exposure compared with the attended path, without a stated need.
  - **Recommended fix:** Unset it after validation in both modes. Pass it explicitly only to the specific step that needs it (for example, the readiness `op-cli-auth` probe).
- **Retry classifier scans entire command output**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`
  - **Lines:** `installer_output_is_transient`
  - **Problem:** The patterns run over the full stdout and stderr of long delegates such as `install-agent-os-runtime.sh` and `brew bundle`. Any benign `timeout`/`502`/`ECONNREFUSED` text anywhere in the output reruns the whole delegate after an unrelated hard failure. Conversely, any benign `No such file or directory` line suppresses a legitimate transient retry.
  - **Why it matters:** Retry behavior on long runs becomes hard to predict. Rerunning the entire runtime installer is only safe if every step is truly idempotent.
  - **Recommended fix:** Classify the tail of stderr (for example, the last N lines), or the final error block, rather than the entire capture.
- **Exported `sudo` wrapper with `--preserve-env` leaks into child producers**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`
  - **Lines:** `installer_unattended_functions` (`export -f sudo git`)
  - **Problem:** The exported function is inherited by every child bash, including `pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh`'s `sudo -n -l` probe, whose message the adapter requires to start with "sudo authorized non-interactively". Under a restrictive sudoers policy (no SETENV / not `ALL`), the `--preserve-env=<list>` can be rejected, which would fail the probe or later privileged commands. The lab's sudoers shape is unspecified, so this is uncertain.
  - **Why it matters:** Readiness or privileged steps could fail for a reason unrelated to the host's actual state.
  - **Recommended fix:** Document the required sudoers shape (SETENV or `ALL`), or drop `--preserve-env` for list, validate, and query modes.
- **Attended-mode behavior changes beyond unattended scope**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/install-agent-os.sh`, `bootstrap/install.sh`, `bootstrap/bootstrap.sh`
  - **Lines:** `install_harnesses` (fatal bundle, now always runs); `install.sh` preflight moved after `phase_1_apps`; `bootstrap.sh` closed-stdin refusal; runtime install moved from 4.25 to 5.9
  - **Problem:** Several changes apply to attended runs too:
    - Wrapper `brew bundle` failures (for example, casks needing interactive acceptance) are now fatal.
    - `--preflight --phase-1-apps` now mutates before preflight.
    - Attended `bootstrap.sh` with non-tty stdin now refuses.
    - The runtime install surface now runs after the 1Password, broker, and keychain-bridge steps.
  - **Why it matters:** These are intended hardening, but they are operator-visible changes to attended flows and are only documented in the TIH README.
  - **Recommended fix:** Note them in `bootstrap/AGENTS.md` and the fresh-Mac runbook.
- **Homebrew PgBouncer disable now gated behind readiness**
  - **File:** `bootstrap/bootstrap.sh`
  - **Lines:** 5.9 block (`disable_homebrew_pgbouncer_service` after precheck)
  - **Problem:** If readiness refuses, the duplicate Homebrew PgBouncer service is never disabled. An existing `homebrew.mxcl.pgbouncer` holding 6432 also makes readiness report `warn:port-6432`, so the step that would fix the conflict never runs.
  - **Why it matters:** This compounds the blocking re-entrancy issue above.
  - **Recommended fix:** Run the duplicate-service removal before the readiness probe, or treat it as part of the expected-holder reconciliation.

## Suggested fixes
- Make unattended readiness re-entrant: allowlist self-owned canonical listeners, or skip/record readiness per attempt. Add a rerun fixture in which the canonical ports are held.
- Write a global Git identity from `AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME/EMAIL` before the precheck. Require or explicitly exclude `op-cli-auth` when no agent workspace is selected.
- Invoke the adapter with `${HQ_PYTHON3:-python3}` and check that the version is at least 3.11.
- Unset `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` after validation in unattended mode as well.
- Classify only the tail of stderr in `installer_output_is_transient`.
- Move `disable_homebrew_pgbouncer_service` ahead of the readiness probe.
- Update `bootstrap/AGENTS.md` and the fresh-Mac runbook for the new `--non-interactive` contract and the attended-mode ordering and fatality changes.

## Verdict
Request changes

## Adversarial Review — Gemini (gemini-reviewer-lacey)

> Reviewer: gemini · Gemini 3.1 Pro (High) · none

## Summary
Reviewed the unattended installation mode additions and retry wrappers across the bootstrap toolchain. The implementation adheres to the required operational patterns: transient `launchctl` and network errors are classified and retried using the final 20 lines of stderr (avoiding the `.splitlines()[0]` truncation hazard), subprocess output buffering is restricted to non-interactive mode to preserve streaming output for attended runs, and cross-user operations (`mkdir`, `tee`, `git clone`) correctly enforce identity boundaries via `sudo -u`. The introduction of the `readiness-v1` checkpoint ensures re-entrancy for partial failures.

## Blocking issues
- None.

## Non-blocking issues
- None.

## Suggested fixes
- None.

## Verdict
Comment only

[codex] CODEXRELOGIN-01: `hq broker relogin codex` runs the whole recovery and sends the operator the device code (#8129)

## Summary

Adds an attended, end-to-end Codex recovery command that prints and pages the device link/code, then publishes and verifies the recovered grant through the fleet. The operator only needs to approve the device code.



## What changed

Adds oauth_broker.relogin and hq broker relogin codex [--check-only]. Recovery backs up admin credentials, uses bounded device login and the existing Sentinel page channel, loads/kicks the root mirror, waits for file agreement and both brokers' Codex can_serve, syncs as runtime owner, compares worker/broker access hashes and runs an ephemeral smoke. Noninteractive sudo identifies unavailable user switching without prompting. Updates RUNBOOK-broker-ops.md and permanent-refresh failure pages; adds fake-binary recovery tests and page-text regression coverage. No CI checks, gates, config keys or workflows added.

Claude-code follow-up would need bridge-owner login (rather than Codex device auth), the Claude keychain/bridge publication path, Claude-specific credential inspection and worker token consumption, plus Claude broker readiness and smoke verification. This PR implements only Codex.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 left Codex unavailable for 69 minutes and recovery required rediscovering the credential publication and worker-sync sequence. Builds on PR 8106, PR 8108 and PR 8109. Operator: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". When recovery initially waited for intervention, the operator said: "You have the tools you don't need operator intervention. It has been done before." This command starts recovery and delivers the approval request directly, while keeping upstream refresh tokens out of worker files and out of output.


## Post-merge activities

Normal main-catchup deployment makes the hq command available. Deploy the updated watchdog through its documented operator restart path so future permanent-refresh pages name the recovery command. No live recovery or restarts were performed by this worker.

## Ticket
CODEXRELOGIN-01

## Spec
none

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

22 scoped tests passed: 17 isolated recovery tests, four selected permanent-refresh page regressions and CLI reference parity. Stand-in Codex/launchctl/pager/sync binaries and temporary fake auth/log files verify order, repeatability, failure stops, timeout handling, noninteractive user switching, no-op check-only, token redaction and safe mirror-direction reporting; stand-in HTTP broker covers serving Codex despite aggregate HTTP 503. Ruff check/format, git diff --check and shellcheck gate passed. Initial managed push correctly rejected stale CLI reference; regenerated the reference and its parity test passes. No full worker-pool suite or live auth/page/service operations. Managed exact-head push succeeded with budget-deferred attestation after its two automatic budget overruns; GitHub CI and AMA must be green before merge.

## Out-of-scope changes

(none)

commit.message:
[codex] ROLLGUARD-01: a broker roll is announced, waits out a refresh, and is verified provider by provider (#8130)

## Summary

Deploy broker recreates now record both brokers before and after, wait for observed refresh activity to settle, announce the roll on the existing ledger event surface, and verify serving providers and grant times. A failed verification pages with the exact difference, preserves the standby, and suppresses subsequent automatic recreates.



## What changed

Main-catchup owns the roll wrapper and deploy record, with a 300-second quiet-window wait budget and a 120-second post-command verification budget; individual status probes are bounded to five seconds. Both launcher recreate paths use it. Image-drift convergence recreates only the primary, leaving the standby running. Additive broker /readyz fields expose per-grant refresh time and hash prefix, refresh ages, and in-flight refresh observations including direct credential leases. The session-ledger event allowlist registers the two announcements using existing phases and statuses. Image equality repairs the persisted drift receipt. No config.yaml keys, CI checks, ratchets, override labels, or new fail-closed auth conditions were added.

Limits: timing uses status observations; a refresh can start between the last observation and recreate, so this is not an atomic refresh reservation. The reported unavailability duration is explicitly an upper bound from recreate start to verification. A pre-upgrade broker has no grant-status fields: its initial empty grant snapshot cannot prove grant continuity, and the native standby must load the additive status code before subsequent rolls have complete grant evidence on both instances. These limitations are recorded in the walkthrough rather than presented as stronger guarantees.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 showed that a silent deploy could load a rolled-back grant while workers were in flight. Operator, verbatim: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". This complements PR 8106 (grant-aware mirror), PR 8108 (broker grant monotonicity), and PR 8109 (auth paging and builder holds), with deploy evidence and provider-by-provider outcome verification. The existing grant store remains the protection against an actual rollback; this change makes the deployment and any observed regression visible.


## Post-merge activities

The deploy of this pull request rolls the broker. Normal main-catchup propagation activates the wrapper and primary status fields; use the normal operator-managed standby activation path for its additive status fields, while preserving standby service during primary rolls. No config migration is needed. After a failed verification, investigate and recover the exact provider/grant difference before removing the failed roll record to re-enable automatic rolls. No live host actions were performed by this worker.

ROLLGUARD-01

none

pr

(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

14 scoped main-catchup tests passed (roll and image drift); 76 broker auth-file/token-cache unit tests passed in the declared test environment; one fake-provider /readyz integration test passed (47 unrelated endpoint tests deselected). Launcher and broker-image-drift shell tests returned zero; the existing completion guard records its known CLZ-01 skip for the launcher suite tail. Ruff lint/format, shellcheck gate, docs linkcheck and git diff --check passed. Tests used temporary directories, fake credentials/providers, and stubbed alert seams. Managed git-safe push accepted the final head as budget-deferred after its built-in retry; GitHub CI and AMA still gate merge.

[codex] ROLLGUARD-01: a broker roll is announced, waits out a refresh, and is verified provider by provider (#8130)

## Summary

Deploy broker recreates now record both brokers before and after, wait for observed refresh activity to settle, announce the roll on the existing ledger event surface, and verify serving providers and grant times. A failed verification pages with the exact difference, preserves the standby, and suppresses subsequent automatic recreates.



## What changed

Main-catchup owns the roll wrapper and deploy record, with a 300-second quiet-window wait budget and a 120-second post-command verification budget; individual status probes are bounded to five seconds. Both launcher recreate paths use it. Image-drift convergence recreates only the primary, leaving the standby running. Additive broker /readyz fields expose per-grant refresh time and hash prefix, refresh ages, and in-flight refresh observations including direct credential leases. The session-ledger event allowlist registers the two announcements using existing phases and statuses. Image equality repairs the persisted drift receipt. No config.yaml keys, CI checks, ratchets, override labels, or new fail-closed auth conditions were added.

Limits: timing uses status observations; a refresh can start between the last observation and recreate, so this is not an atomic refresh reservation. The reported unavailability duration is explicitly an upper bound from recreate start to verification. A pre-upgrade broker has no grant-status fields: its initial empty grant snapshot cannot prove grant continuity, and the native standby must load the additive status code before subsequent rolls have complete grant evidence on both instances. These limitations are recorded in the walkthrough rather than presented as stronger guarantees.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 showed that a silent deploy could load a rolled-back grant while workers were in flight. Operator, verbatim: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". This complements PR 8106 (grant-aware mirror), PR 8108 (broker grant monotonicity), and PR 8109 (auth paging and builder holds), with deploy evidence and provider-by-provider outcome verification. The existing grant store remains the protection against an actual rollback; this change makes the deployment and any observed regression visible.


## Post-merge activities

The deploy of this pull request rolls the broker. Normal main-catchup propagation activates the wrapper and primary status fields; use the normal operator-managed standby activation path for its additive status fields, while preserving standby service during primary rolls. No config migration is needed. After a failed verification, investigate and recover the exact provider/grant difference before removing the failed roll record to re-enable automatic rolls. No live host actions were performed by this worker.

Launcher and broker-image-drift shell tests returned zero; the existing completion guard records its known CLZ-01 skip for the launcher suite tail. Ruff lint/format, shellcheck gate, docs linkcheck and git diff --check passed. Tests used temporary directories, fake credentials/providers, and stubbed alert seams. +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared, opt-in prompt refusal for the reached installer chain.
+installer_unattended_init() {
+  case "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" in
+    0) return 0 ;;
+    1) ;;
+    *) printf 'unattended-input: AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE must be 0 or 1\n' >&2; return 64 ;;
+  esac
+  set +x +v
+  export AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 CI=1 GH_ASSUME_YES=1
+  export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  export SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  # Ignore a supplied interactive SSH command: unattended cannot inherit an agent
+  # or password prompt. Host verification remains enabled.
+  export GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oIdentityAgent=none -oBatchMode=yes -oConnectTimeout=15 -oServerAliveInterval=15 -oServerAliveCountMax=3'
+  export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1
+  exec </dev/null
+}
+
+installer_unattended_sudo_check() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  [[ "$(id -u)" == 0 ]] && return 0
+  command sudo -n true || {
+    printf 'unattended-input: pre-authorized noninteractive sudo required\n' >&2
+    return 77
+  }
+}
+
+# Functions preserve attended argv exactly. Export only in unattended mode so
+# reached Bash helpers also refuse askpass. sudo policies still authorize every
+# operation; a cached timestamp is never treated as an enduring grant.
+installer_unattended_functions() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  sudo() {
+    local arg args=()
+    for arg in "$@"; do
+      [[ "$arg" == -A ]] || args+=("$arg")
+    done
+    command sudo -n --preserve-env=AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE,GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT,GIT_ASKPASS,SSH_ASKPASS,GIT_SSH_COMMAND,GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME,GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL,GIT_COMMITTER_NAME,GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL,SUDO_ASKPASS "${args[@]}"
+  }
+  git() {
+    local identity=()
+    if [[ -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" && -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+      identity=(-c "user.name=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" -c "user.email=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL")
+    fi
+    command git "${identity[@]}" -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=/usr/bin/false \
+      -c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0 -c fetch.writeCommitGraph=false "$@"
+  }
+  export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'credential.helper=' 'core.askPass=/usr/bin/false' 'maintenance.auto=false' 'gc.auto=0' 'fetch.writeCommitGraph=false'"
+  export -f sudo git
+}
+
+installer_unattended_core_inputs() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: acknowledge unsupported OAuth/Keychain with AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  if [[ -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: explicit AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME and AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL required\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME"
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL"
+}
+
+# Only idempotent provisioning operations belong here. Unknown and structural
+# failures stop immediately; a transient signature never overrides an auth,
+# permission, certificate-verification or configuration error in the same run.
+installer_output_is_transient() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if grep -Eiq 'permission denied|operation not permitted|authentication failed|could not read (username|password)|repository .*not found|repository not found|host key verification failed|certificate verify failed|certificate verification failed|unable to get local issuer certificate|self.signed certificate|invalid (argument|configuration|plist)|no such file or directory|EACCES|EPERM|E401|E403' "$@"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$kind" == runtime ]] && grep -Eiq 'bootstrap failed: 5: input/output error|(^|[^[:alnum:]_])EIO([^[:alnum:]_]|$)|resource temporarily unavailable|service not yet bootstrapped' "$@"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  grep -Eiq 'timed out|timeout|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|EAI_AGAIN|connection reset|connection refused|temporary failure in name resolution|could not resolve host|could not resolve hostname|TLS handshake|SSL.*(connect|handshake)|early EOF|remote end hung up unexpectedly|HTTP[^[:digit:]]+50[234]|(error|response|returned)[^[:digit:]]+50[234]' "$@"
+}
+
+installer_run_with_retry() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  local capture_dir attempt status delay
+  capture_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return 1
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    status=0
+    "$@" >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" || status=$?
+    cat "$capture_dir/stdout"
+    cat "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2
+    if [[ "$status" == 0 ]]; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! installer_output_is_transient "$kind" "$capture_dir/stdout" "$capture_dir/stderr"; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return "$status"
+    fi
+    # Fixed provisioning policy, matching the launchd post-bootout recovery
+    # window. No exponential arithmetic or retry tuning inputs to duplicate.
+    case "$attempt" in 1) delay=2 ;; 2) delay=5 ;; esac
+    printf 'unattended-retry: %s transient failure on attempt %s/3; retrying in %ss\n' "$kind" "$attempt" "$delay" >&2
+    sleep "$delay"
+  done
+}
+
+# Existing producer + TIH-01 strict adapter, before launchd mutations. No auth
+# probe is executed on the builder host; callers run this only in the lab install.
+installer_unattended_precheck() {
+  local repo_root="$1" stage="$2" timeout_seconds="${3:-120}"
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  python3 - "$repo_root" "$stage" "$timeout_seconds" <<'PYCODE'
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+stage = sys.argv[2]
+try:
+    timeout_seconds = float(sys.argv[3])
+    if not 0 < timeout_seconds <= 120:
+        raise ValueError
+except ValueError:
+    print("unattended-input: precheck timeout must be positive and at most 120 seconds", file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(64)
+sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "modules/test-install-host"))
+from checks import adapt
+from contracts import Stage
+
+
+def preserve_stderr(diagnostics):
+    # Raw producer output can include auth identity. Keep it out of the public
+    # installer log, but leave a mode-0600 file for the invoking operator.
+    if diagnostics:
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
+            mode="w", prefix="agent-os-precheck-", suffix=".stderr", delete=False
+        ) as diagnostic_file:
+            diagnostic_file.write(diagnostics)
+        print(f"unattended-input: precheck stderr saved to {diagnostic_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+process = subprocess.Popen(
+    ["bash", str(root / "scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh"), "--json"],
+    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, start_new_session=True,
+)
+try:
+    raw, diagnostics = process.communicate(timeout=timeout_seconds)
+except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+    _, diagnostics = process.communicate()
+    preserve_stderr(diagnostics)
+    print("unattended-input: precheck timed out", file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(124)
+coverage = adapt("precheck", raw, stage=Stage(stage),
+                 boot_id="installer-precheck", exit_code=process.returncode)
+if not coverage.qualified:
+    preserve_stderr(diagnostics)
+# Normalized reasons contain check IDs only; raw identity/auth messages are not
+# forwarded into the installer log. Actual boot provenance belongs to TIH-05.
+print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "qualified": coverage.qualified,
+                  "reasons": coverage.reasons}))
+sys.exit(0 if coverage.qualified else 1)
+PYCODE
+}
+
+installer_brew_bundle() {
+  local brew_bin="$1" brewfile="$2" temporary_file status
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$brewfile" --no-lock
+    return
+  fi
+  temporary_file="$(mktemp)" || return 1
+  # Preserve the canonical formula inventory and CLI casks only.
+  awk '$1 != "cask" || $2 == "\"1password-cli\"" || $2 == "\"claude-code\"" || $2 == "\"codex\"" { print }' \
+    "$brewfile" >"$temporary_file" || { rm -f "$temporary_file"; return 1; }
+  printf 'brew "colima"\nbrew "docker"\nbrew "docker-compose"\n' >>"$temporary_file"
+  status=0
+  installer_run_with_retry network "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$temporary_file" --no-lock || status=$?
+  rm -f "$temporary_file"
+  [[ "$status" == 0 ]] || {
+    printf 'dependency provisioning failed; refusing partial install\n' >&2
+    return "$status"
+  }
+  printf 'coverage-excluded: protected GUI casks (LuLu/TCC, Docker Desktop, desktop applications)\n' >&2
+}

+            ("operation now in progress", "cannot connect to the docker daemon"),
+            (r"bootstrap failed: 5\b",),
+        )
+    return isinstance(exc, OSError) and exc.errno in {errno.EIO, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EBUSY}
+
+
+def _recreate(command):
+    # Keep command diagnostics without a pipe that can hide successful progress.
+    with tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+", encoding="utf-8") as stderr:
+        try:
+            return subprocess.run(command, check=True, timeout=310, stderr=stderr, text=True)
+        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            exc.stderr = stderr.read()
+            raise
+        finally:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            sys.stderr.write(stderr.read())
+            sys.stderr.flush()
+
+
+def snapshot(url):
+    try:
+        response = urllib.request.urlopen(url + "/readyz", timeout=5)
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+        response = exc  # A 503 still carries provider and grant evidence.
+    with response:
+        body = json.load(response)
+    return {
+        "provider_states": body.get("provider_states", {}),
+        "grants": body.get("grants", {}),
+        "refresh_in_flight": body.get("refresh_in_flight", False),
+    }
+
+
+def _serving_providers(states):
+    return {
+        provider
+        for body in states.values()
+        for provider, state in body.get("provider_states", {}).items()
+        if state.get("can_serve")
+    }
+
+
+def _standby_preflight(states):
+    standby = states.get("standby", {})
+    if not standby or standby.get("observationError"):
+        return ["standby: status observation unavailable"]
+    if not _serving_providers({"standby": standby}):
+        return ["standby: no serving providers observed"]
+    return [
+        f"standby provider {provider}: cannot cover primary during recreate"
+        for provider in sorted(_serving_providers(states))
+        if not standby.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve")
+    ]
+
+
+def differences(before, after):
+    result = []
+    serving = _serving_providers(before)
+    for broker, previous in before.items():
+        current = after.get(broker, {})
+        if current.get("observationError"):
+            result.append(f"{broker}: status observation unavailable")
+            continue
+        for provider in serving:
+            if not current.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve"):
+                result.append(f"{broker} provider {provider}: can_serve true -> false/missing")
+        for grant, state in previous.get("grants", {}).items():
+            new = current.get("grants", {}).get(grant, {})
+            if new.get("last_refresh", -1) < state["last_refresh"]:
+                result.append(
+                    f"{broker} grant {grant}: last_refresh {state['last_refresh']} -> {new.get('last_refresh', 'missing')}"
+                )
+    return result
+
+
+def quiet(states):
+    if any(body.get("refresh_in_flight") for body in states.values()):
+        return False
+    if any(
+        grant.get("seconds_since_last_refresh", QUIET_SECONDS) < QUIET_SECONDS
+        for body in states.values()
+        for grant in body.get("grants", {}).values()
+    ):
+        return False
+    return all(
+        not state.get("refresh_in_flight")
+        and (
+            state.get("refresh_age_measured_from") != "last_refresh"
+            or state.get("seconds_since_last_refresh", 0) >= QUIET_SECONDS
+        )
+        for body in states.values()
+        for state in body.get("provider_states", {}).values()
+    )
+
+
+def roll(
+    *,
+    read,
+    recreate,
+    record,
+    emit,
+    page,
+    reason,
+    prs,
+    clock=time.monotonic,
+    sleep=time.sleep,
+    wait_seconds=WAIT_SECONDS,
+    verify_seconds=VERIFY_SECONDS,
+):
+    start = clock()
+    before = read()
+    while not quiet(before) and clock() - start < wait_seconds:
+        sleep(min(POLL_SECONDS, max(0, wait_seconds - (clock() - start))))
+        before = read()
+    evidence = {
+        "rollId": uuid.uuid4().hex,
+        "reason": reason,
+        "prs": prs,
+        "before": before,
+        "waitSeconds": clock() - start,
+        "waitBoundSeconds": wait_seconds,
+        "waitBoundReached": not quiet(before),
+        "verifyBoundSeconds": verify_seconds,
+    }
+
+    def announce(kind):
+        try:
+            emit(kind, evidence)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence.setdefault("eventErrors", []).append(type(exc).__name__)
+
+    record(evidence)
+    announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_started")
+    preflight = _standby_preflight(before)
+    if preflight:
+        # No command ran: retain the primary and allow a later health-based retry.
+        evidence.update(
+            after=before,
+            differences=preflight,
+            commandAttempts=0,
+            commandError=None,
+            result="deferred",
+            unavailabilitySeconds=0,
+            unavailabilityMeasurement="no recreate attempted",
+        )
+        record(evidence)
+        announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_finished")
+        record(evidence)
+        return evidence
+    unavailable = clock()
+    error = None
+    for attempt in range(COMMAND_ATTEMPTS):
+        evidence["commandAttempts"] = attempt + 1
+        try:
+            recreate()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            # Timeouts can leave a partially completed recreate: do not replay them.
+            if not _transient_command_error(exc) or attempt == COMMAND_ATTEMPTS - 1:
+                error = type(exc).__name__
+                break
+            sleep(bounded_exponential_delay(attempt, base_seconds=1, max_seconds=2))
+        else:
+            break
+    deadline = clock() + verify_seconds
+    after = read()
+    delta = differences(before, after)
+    while delta and clock() < deadline:
+        sleep(min(POLL_SECONDS, max(0, deadline - clock())))
+        after = read()
+        delta = differences(before, after)
+    evidence.update(
+        after=after,
+        differences=delta,
+        commandError=error,
+        result="failed" if delta or error else "verified",
+        unavailabilitySeconds=clock() - unavailable,
+        unavailabilityMeasurement="upper bound from recreate start to verified status",
+    )
+    record(evidence)
+    announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_finished")
+    record(evidence)
+    if delta or error:
+        try:
+            evidence["pageDelivered"] = bool(page(evidence))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence["pageDelivered"] = False
+            evidence["pageError"] = type(exc).__name__
+        record(evidence)
+    return evidence
+
+
+def event_status(evidence):
+    result = evidence.get("result", "running")
+    return {"verified": "succeeded", "deferred": "warning"}.get(result, result)
+
+
+def _number(name, default):
+    try:
+        value = float(os.environ.get(name, default))
+        return value if math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0 else default
+    except ValueError:
+        return default
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--reason", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("command", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    from agent_os_config.roots import hq_root_preferring_legacy_env
+    from main_catchup import stateio
+    from main_catchup.broker_image_drift import _write_state
+    from main_catchup.broker_image_drift import _prepare_state_parent
+
+    root = Path(hq_root_preferring_legacy_env())
+    history = root / "main-catchup/broker-roll.json"
+    try:
+        _prepare_state_parent(history, owner_root=root)
+    except OSError:
+        return 75  # Never recreate when the durable failure guard cannot be owned safely.
+    # Failed verification suppresses automatic repeats across launcher processes.
+    try:
+        prior = json.loads(history.read_text())
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        prior = {}
+    urls = {
+        "primary": os.environ.get("BROKER_ROLL_PRIMARY_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4099"),
+        "standby": os.environ.get("BROKER_ROLL_STANDBY_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4097"),
+    }
+
+    def read():
+        result = {}
+        for name, url in urls.items():
+            try:
+                result[name] = snapshot(url)
+            except (OSError, ValueError):
+                result[name] = {"provider_states": {}, "grants": {}, "observationError": True}
+        return result
+
+    def record(evidence):
+        # The suppression record is mandatory; do not roll without durable evidence.
+        _write_state(history, evidence, owner_root=root)
+        try:
+            # stateio locks as the directory owner and preserves HQ ownership for root.
+            stateio._write_state(root, brokerRoll=evidence)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence.setdefault("recordErrors", []).append(type(exc).__name__)
+
+    def emit(kind, evidence):
+        from main_catchup.daemon import _append_audit_event
+        from session_ledger.db import LedgerDatabase
+        from session_ledger.db_path import resolve_ledger_target
+
+        target = resolve_ledger_target(hq_root=root, module_anchor=args.repo)
+        db = LedgerDatabase(target.db_path)
+        try:
+            _append_audit_event(
+                db,
+                args.repo,
+                kind,
+                summary=args.reason,
+                payload=evidence,
+                status=event_status(evidence),
+                phase="operating",
+            )
+        finally:
+            db.close()
+
+    def page(evidence):
+        # Same auth page delivery helper as PR 8109; keep the deploy wrapper
+        # independent of the broker's aiohttp/metrics runtime dependencies.
+        subprocess.run(
+            [
+                os.environ.get("SENTINEL_NODE_BIN", "node"),
+                str(args.repo / "scripts/alert-delivery.mjs"),
+                "--message",
+                "OAuth broker deploy roll failed: "
+                + "; ".join(evidence["differences"] or [evidence["commandError"]]),
+                "--source",
+                "oauth-broker",
+                "--idempotency-key",
+                "oauth-broker:auth:roll:" + evidence["rollId"],
+                "--metadata-json",
+                json.dumps(
+                    {"alertKey": "broker:auth:roll", "priority": "critical", "roll": evidence}
+                ),
+                "--rate-limit-seconds",
+                "900",
+            ],
+            check=True,
+            timeout=20,
+            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        )
+        return True
+
+    if prior.get("result") == "failed":
+        if not prior.get("pageDelivered"):
+            try:
+                prior["pageDelivered"] = bool(page(prior))
+            except Exception as exc:
+                prior["pageError"] = type(exc).__name__
+            record(prior)
+        return 75
+
+    command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == ["--"] else args.command
+    deploy_range = stateio._read_state(root).get("lastFFRange") or {}
+    revisions = (
+        [f"{deploy_range['fromSha']}..{deploy_range['toSha']}"]
+        if deploy_range.get("fromSha") and deploy_range.get("toSha")
+        else ["-1"]
+    )
+    try:
+        subjects = subprocess.run(
+            [
+                "git",
+                "-C",
+                str(args.repo),
+                "log",
+                *revisions,
+                "--format=%s",
+                "--",
+                "platform/oauth-broker",
+                "modules/model-routing-budget-control/runtime",
+            ],
+            check=True,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=10,
+        ).stdout
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+        print(
+            f"broker-roll: merged PR attribution unavailable ({type(exc).__name__})",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        subjects = ""
+    prs = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\(#(\d+)\)", subjects)))
+    result = roll(
+        read=read,
+        recreate=lambda: _recreate(command),
+        record=record,
+        emit=emit,
+        page=page,
+        reason=args.reason,
+        prs=prs,
+        wait_seconds=_number("BROKER_ROLL_WAIT_SECONDS", WAIT_SECONDS),
+        verify_seconds=_number("BROKER_ROLL_VERIFY_SECONDS", VERIFY_SECONDS),
+    )
+    return 0 if result["result"] == "verified" else 75
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
