+"""ROLLGUARD-01, entirely fake status, clocks, commands, records and pager."""
+
+from copy import deepcopy
+import errno
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from main_catchup import broker_roll
+
+
+def baseline():
+    return {
+        broker: {
+            "provider_states": {
+                "codex": {
+                    "can_serve": True,
+                    "refresh_in_flight": False,
+                    "refresh_age_measured_from": "last_refresh",
+                    "seconds_since_last_refresh": 180,
+                }
+            },
+            "grants": {"codex": {"last_refresh": 100, "fingerprint_prefix": "12345678"}},
+        }
+        for broker in ("primary", "standby")
+    }
+
+
+def exercise(before=None, after=None, wait=10):
+    now = [0]
+    reads = [0]
+    events, records, pages, recreates = [], [], [], []
+
+    def read():
+        reads[0] += 1
+        if recreates:
+            return deepcopy(after or baseline())
+        return deepcopy(before if before is not None and reads[0] == 1 else baseline())
+
+    def sleep(seconds):
+        now[0] += seconds
+
+    result = broker_roll.roll(
+        read=read,
+        recreate=lambda: recreates.append(now[0]),
+        record=lambda r: records.append(deepcopy(r)),
+        emit=lambda *e: events.append(deepcopy(e)),
+        page=pages.append,
+        reason="image-drift",
+        prs=["8109"],
+        clock=lambda: now[0],
+        sleep=sleep,
+        wait_seconds=wait,
+        verify_seconds=4,
+    )
+    return result, records, events, pages, recreates
+
+
+def test_refresh_in_flight_delays_recreate():
+    before = baseline()
+    before["primary"]["provider_states"]["codex"]["refresh_in_flight"] = True
+    result, _, _, _, recreates = exercise(before)
+    assert recreates == [2]
+    assert not result["waitBoundReached"]
+
+
+def test_recent_refresh_delays_recreate():
+    before = baseline()
+    before["primary"]["provider_states"]["codex"]["seconds_since_last_refresh"] = 119
+    assert exercise(before)[4] == [2]
+
+
+def test_lost_provider_pages_exact_name():
+    after = baseline()
+    after["primary"]["provider_states"] = {}
+    result, _, _, pages, recreates = exercise(after=after)
+    assert "primary provider codex" in pages[0]["differences"][0]
+    assert result["result"] == "failed"
+    assert len(recreates) == 1
+
+
+def test_older_grant_pages():
+    after = baseline()
+    after["standby"]["grants"]["codex"]["last_refresh"] = 99
+    assert "100 -> 99" in exercise(after=after)[3][0]["differences"][0]
+
+
+def test_healthy_roll_records_snapshots_and_both_events():
+    result, records, events, pages, _ = exercise()
+    assert result["result"] == "verified"
+    assert records[0]["before"] == baseline()
+    assert records[1]["after"] == baseline()
+    assert [e[0] for e in events] == [
+        "main_catchup.broker_roll_started",
+        "main_catchup.broker_roll_finished",
+    ]
+    assert not pages
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("standby", [None, {"observationError": True}, {"provider_states": {}}])
+def test_unverifiable_standby_defers_without_recreate_or_failure_latch(standby):
+    before = baseline()
+    if standby is None:
+        del before["standby"]
+    else:
+        before["standby"] = standby
+    result, records, events, pages, recreates = exercise(before)
+    assert not recreates
+    assert not pages
+    assert result["result"] == records[-1]["result"] == "deferred"
+    assert result["commandAttempts"] == 0
+    assert result["unavailabilitySeconds"] == 0
+    assert result["differences"]
+    assert len(events) == 2
+
+
+def test_standby_must_cover_every_previously_serving_provider():
+    before = baseline()
+    before["primary"]["provider_states"]["gemini"] = {"can_serve": True}
+    result, _, _, pages, recreates = exercise(before)
+    assert not recreates
+    assert not pages
+    assert result["result"] == "deferred"
+    assert "standby provider gemini" in result["differences"][0]
+
+
+def test_preflight_checks_the_last_snapshot_after_quiet_wait():
+    busy = baseline()
+    busy["primary"]["refresh_in_flight"] = True
+    unavailable = baseline()
+    unavailable["standby"] = {"observationError": True}
+    observations = iter([busy, unavailable])
+    now = [0]
+
+    def forbidden(*_):
+        pytest.fail("preflight deferral must not recreate or page")
+
+    result = broker_roll.roll(
+        read=lambda: next(observations),
+        recreate=forbidden,
+        record=lambda _: None,
+        emit=lambda *_: None,
+        page=forbidden,
+        reason="image-drift",
+        prs=[],
+        clock=lambda: now[0],
+        sleep=lambda s: now.__setitem__(0, now[0] + s),
+    )
+    assert result["result"] == "deferred"
+    assert result["waitSeconds"] == 2
+
+
+def test_recovered_primary_verifies_without_paging_or_failure_latch():
+    before = baseline()
+    before["primary"] = {"observationError": True}

+"""Configure legacy LiteLLM OTEL without its parentless service-hook failure.
+
+v1.88.2 ServiceLogging.async_log_success_event drops the request timestamps
+and parent. Legacy OpenTelemetry converts those timestamps before checking
+whether it has a parent, although it only emits service spans with a parent.
+The caller-side parent gate was removed in upstream PR 28909 (2026-05-30).
+Our watchdog exercises this path every 60 seconds via its chat probe.
+Request hooks and parented service spans remain owned by upstream OpenTelemetry.
+"""
+
+from litellm.integrations.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetry
+
+
+class ServiceTelemetry(OpenTelemetry):
+    async def async_service_success_hook(
+        self,
+        payload,
+        parent_otel_span=None,
+        start_time=None,
+        end_time=None,
+        event_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        if parent_otel_span is None:
+            return
+        await super().async_service_success_hook(
+            payload=payload,
+            parent_otel_span=parent_otel_span,
+            start_time=start_time,
+            end_time=end_time,
+            event_metadata=event_metadata,
+        )
+
+    async def async_service_failure_hook(
+        self,
+        payload,
+        error="",
+        parent_otel_span=None,
+        start_time=None,
+        end_time=None,
+        event_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        # The sibling failure hook has the same convert-before-parent pattern.
+        if parent_otel_span is None:
+            return
+        await super().async_service_failure_hook(
+            payload=payload,
+            error=error,
+            parent_otel_span=parent_otel_span,
+            start_time=start_time,
+            end_time=end_time,
+            event_metadata=event_metadata,
+        )
+
+
+proxy_handler_instance = ServiceTelemetry()

+"""Offline v1.88.2 hook excerpts (MIT, BerriAI/litellm).
+
+Source: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/a0d05ba257c27682c1d2dfcb995d53b00a5bd3c3
+Only imports/annotations are stubbed by the test; hook bodies are unchanged.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from datetime import timedelta
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+ServiceTypes = SimpleNamespace(LITELLM="self")
+litellm = SimpleNamespace(service_callback=[])
+verbose_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class OpenTelemetry:
+    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
+        self._handle_success(kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time)
+
+    async def async_service_success_hook(
+        self, payload, parent_otel_span=None, start_time=None, end_time=None, event_metadata=None
+    ):
+        from opentelemetry import trace
+        from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode
+
+        _start_time_ns = 0
+        _end_time_ns = 0
+        if isinstance(start_time, float):
+            _start_time_ns = int(start_time * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _start_time_ns = self._to_ns(start_time)
+        if isinstance(end_time, float):
+            _end_time_ns = int(end_time * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _end_time_ns = self._to_ns(end_time)
+        if parent_otel_span is not None:
+            _span_name = payload.service
+            service_logging_span = self.tracer.start_span(
+                name=_span_name,
+                context=trace.set_span_in_context(parent_otel_span),
+                start_time=_start_time_ns,
+            )
+            self.safe_set_attribute(
+                span=service_logging_span, key="call_type", value=payload.call_type
+            )
+            self.safe_set_attribute(
+                span=service_logging_span, key="service", value=payload.service.value
+            )
+            if event_metadata:
+                for key, value in event_metadata.items():
+                    if value is None:
+                        value = "None"
+                    if isinstance(value, dict):
+                        try:
+                            value = str(value)
+                        except Exception:
+                            value = "litellm logging error - could_not_json_serialize"
+                    self.safe_set_attribute(span=service_logging_span, key=key, value=value)
+            service_logging_span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.OK))
+            service_logging_span.end(end_time=_end_time_ns)
+
+    async def async_service_failure_hook(
+        self,
+        payload,
+        error="",
+        parent_otel_span=None,
+        start_time=None,
+        end_time=None,
+        event_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        from opentelemetry import trace
+        from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode
+
+        _start_time_ns = 0
+        _end_time_ns = 0
+        if isinstance(start_time, float):
+            _start_time_ns = int(int(start_time) * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _start_time_ns = self._to_ns(start_time)
+        if isinstance(end_time, float):
+            _end_time_ns = int(int(end_time) * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _end_time_ns = self._to_ns(end_time)
+        if parent_otel_span is not None:
+            _span_name = payload.service
+            service_logging_span = self.tracer.start_span(
+                name=_span_name,
+                context=trace.set_span_in_context(parent_otel_span),
+                start_time=_start_time_ns,
+            )
+            self.safe_set_attribute(
+                span=service_logging_span, key="call_type", value=payload.call_type
+            )
+            self.safe_set_attribute(
+                span=service_logging_span, key="service", value=payload.service.value
+            )
+            if error:
+                self.safe_set_attribute(span=service_logging_span, key="error", value=error)
+            if event_metadata:
+                for key, value in event_metadata.items():
+                    if isinstance(value, dict):
+                        try:
+                            value = str(value)
+                        except Exception:
+                            value = "litllm logging error - could_not_json_serialize"
+                    self.safe_set_attribute(span=service_logging_span, key=key, value=value)
+            service_logging_span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.ERROR))
+            service_logging_span.end(end_time=_end_time_ns)
+
+    def _to_ns(self, dt):
+        return int(dt.timestamp() * 1000000000.0)
+
+    def _init_otel_logger_on_litellm_proxy(self):
+        """
+        Initializes OpenTelemetry for litellm proxy server
+
+        - Adds Otel as a service callback
+        - Sets `proxy_server.open_telemetry_logger` to self
+        """
+        try:
+            from litellm.proxy import proxy_server
+        except ImportError:
+            verbose_logger.warning(
+                "Proxy Server is not installed. Skipping OpenTelemetry initialization."
+            )
+            return
+        if "otel" not in litellm.service_callback and all(
+            (not isinstance(cb, OpenTelemetry) for cb in litellm.service_callback)
+        ):
+            litellm.service_callback.append(self)
+        if getattr(proxy_server, "open_telemetry_logger", None) is None:
+            setattr(proxy_server, "open_telemetry_logger", self)
+
+
+class ServiceLogging:
+    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
+        """
+        Hook to track latency for litellm proxy llm api calls
+        """
+        try:
+            _duration = end_time - start_time
+            if isinstance(_duration, timedelta):
+                _duration = _duration.total_seconds()
+            elif isinstance(_duration, float):
+                pass
+            else:
+                raise Exception(
+                    "Duration={} is not a float or timedelta object. type={}".format(
+                        _duration, type(_duration)
+                    )
+                )
+            await self.async_service_success_hook(
+                service=ServiceTypes.LITELLM,
+                duration=_duration,
+                call_type=kwargs.get("call_type", "unknown"),
+            )
+        except Exception as e:
+            raise e

+## TIH-02 unattended installer disposition
+
+The real wrapper accepts `--non-interactive` (or
+`AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`), exports the selection to bootstrap and runtime,
+and closes stdin. Bootstrap and the migration orchestrator also accept this
+flag directly; the runtime installer also accepts the flag and inherits the environment selection.
+Attended topology, account, harness, destination and confirmation defaults
+remain available. No shared CFG leaf, CI check or manifest is added.
+
+A full unattended wrapper/bootstrap invocation requires explicit
+`AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME`, `AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL`, and
+`AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1`. These are install-process inputs, not
+production configuration. Selecting an agent workspace additionally requires
+`OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` before mutation; use only a lab credential provisioned
+by TIH-04. Do not paste credentials into command lines or committed profiles.
+The missing-input prefix is `unattended-input:`; usage/input refusal is nonzero.
+Non-root callers must already have noninteractive sudo authorization. Each
+privileged operation uses `sudo -n`; an initial successful check does not promise
+that later commands are authorized or that a timestamp will remain valid.
+
+Unattended dependency installs (bundle/npm and initial CFG Python/YAML),
+requested clones, Colima/Compose startup, and the idempotent runtime/plist
+install delegates use `bootstrap/lib/unattended.sh`'s classified retry helper.
+Recognized network timeouts/resets, temporary DNS failures, TLS connection or
+handshake failures and HTTP 502/503/504 responses get at most three attempts,
+with fixed 2- then 5-second backoff. Runtime delegates also retry launchd
+bootstrap EIO, temporary resource unavailability and not-yet-bootstrapped
+services. Authentication, permission, certificate verification, missing-file
+and configuration failures stop immediately, as do unrecognized errors;
+exhaustion remains a failed install. Each attempt preserves stdout/stderr and
+prints a retry marker without echoing the command's arguments. These bounds
+cover retry count and delay, not the duration of package-manager operations.
+The wrapper initializes submodules after cloning the parent repository, so a
+transient submodule transfer retries without cloning over a populated checkout.
+The existing `bootstrap/bootstrap.uid-contract.test.sh` CI entrypoint also runs
+`bootstrap/install-agent-os.test.sh`'s unattended retry/refusal fixtures.
+Those fixtures model macOS version, non-root UID, BSD owner lookup and
+connectivity locally, and select the runner's existing account when account
+creation is irrelevant. The Linux CI runner can exercise installer branches
+without a network probe; explicit negative fixtures retain the
+macOS/version/root preflight refusals.
+
+A new dual-mode guest account additionally needs
+`AGENT_OS_RUNTIME_PASSWORD`, `AGENT_OS_ALLOW_SYSADMINCTL_ARGV_PASSWORD=1`, and
+`AGENT_OS_DISPOSABLE_GUEST=1`. This explicitly acknowledges the short-lived
+sysadminctl argv exposure for a disposable guest only. It is never a production
+password or auth mechanism. The installer disables shell tracing in unattended
+mode, does not print the password, and keeps `--runtime-password` forbidden.
+An existing account needs no password. The attended sysadminctl path still uses
+`-password -` and obtains the password directly from the terminal.

+A refusal or exclusion is not a qualified capability. The strict result contract
+continues to reject missing mandatory checks and warnings.

+"""Attended Codex recovery; no subprocess output containing credentials is relayed."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import pwd
+import re
+import selectors
+import shlex
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import time
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from agent_os_config import roots
+from agent_os_config.backoff import bounded_exponential_delay
+from agent_os_config.launchd import safe_resolve_launchd_label_prefix
+
+
+class RecoveryError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class CommandError(RecoveryError):
+    """Keep only classification flags, never raw command output, in exceptions."""
+
+    def __init__(self, message, *, transient=False, service_absent=False):
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.transient = transient
+        self.service_absent = service_absent
+
+
+def command(name, default):
+    return shlex.split(os.environ.get(name, default))
+
+
+def run(argv, timeout=30):
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(
+        argv,
+        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        output, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+        if proc.returncode:
+            diagnostic = output.decode(errors="replace").lower()
+            raise CommandError(
+                "command failed; check permissions and service logs",
+                transient=any(
+                    marker in diagnostic
+                    for marker in (
+                        "input/output error",
+                        "bootstrap failed: 5:",
+                        "resource temporarily unavailable",
+                        "timed out",
+                        "timeout",
+                    )
+                ),
+                service_absent=any(
+                    marker in diagnostic
+                    for marker in (
+                        "could not find service",
+                        "could not find specified service",
+                        "service not found",
+                        "no such process",
+                    )
+                ),
+            )
+        return output
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        raise CommandError(
+            "command timed out; inspect service logs and retry", transient=True
+        ) from None
+    finally:
+        try:
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        except ProcessLookupError:
+            pass
+        proc.wait()
+
+
+def run_launchctl(argv, *, allow_absent=False):
+    """Retry only known transient launchd errors, at most three 30-second attempts."""
+    for attempt in range(3):
+        try:
+            run(argv)
+            return True
+        except CommandError as exc:
+            if allow_absent and exc.service_absent:
+                return False
+            if not exc.transient or attempt == 2:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(bounded_exponential_delay(attempt, base_seconds=1, max_seconds=2))
+
+
+def fingerprint(path, *, user=None):
+    """Read private worker grants as their owner without relaying command output."""
+    try:
+        contents = path.read_text() if user is None else run(user_command(user, ["cat", str(path)]))
+        data = json.loads(contents)
+        token = data["tokens"]["access_token"]
+        return data.get(
+            "last_refresh", data["tokens"].get("fetched_at", "unknown")
+        ), hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
+    except (CommandError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
+        return "unavailable", "unavailable"
+
+
+def mirror_direction(path, offset):
+    """Inspect only this pass's log; never relay raw log contents."""
+    try:
+        with path.open("rb") as log:
+            log.seek(0, 2)
+            end = log.tell()
+            log.seek(max(offset if end >= offset else 0, end - 65536))
+            text = log.read(65536).decode(errors="replace")
+        directions = re.findall(r'"direction":\s*"(src->dst|dst->src)"', text)
+        return directions[-1] if directions else "no copy logged (files agree)"
+    except OSError:
+        return "log unavailable; verified by access hashes"
+
+
+def user_command(user, argv):
+    if pwd.getpwuid(os.geteuid()).pw_name == user:
+        return argv
+    return command("HQ_RELOGIN_SUDO", "sudo") + ["-n", "-H", "-u", user] + argv
+
+
+def ready(url):
+    try:
+        response = urllib.request.urlopen(url + "/readyz", timeout=5)
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+        response = exc
+    with response:
+        return (
+            json.load(response).get("provider_states", {}).get("codex", {}).get("can_serve") is True
+        )
+
+
+def wait_for(predicate, seconds):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
+    while True:
+        try:
+            if predicate():
+                return
+        except Exception:
+            # Polling failures include HTTP protocol errors and malformed response shapes.
+            # Retry without relaying arbitrary exception text; interrupts still propagate.
+            pass
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            raise RecoveryError("wait timed out; inspect mirror and broker logs, then retry")
+        time.sleep(min(1, max(0, deadline - time.monotonic())))
+
+
+def device_login(argv, pager, seconds):
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(
+        argv,
+        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()

+    sent = False
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds

+                    print(message, flush=True)
+                    run(
+                        pager
+                        + [
+                            "--message",
+                            message,
+                            "--source-job-id",
+                            "codex-relogin",
+                            "--metadata-json",
+                            json.dumps(
+                                {
+                                    "title": "Codex login approval",
+                                    "priority": "critical",
+                                    "actionRequired": True,
+                                }
+                            ),
+                        ]
+                    )
+                    sent = True
+            if proc.poll() is not None:
+                if proc.returncode or not sent:
+                    raise RecoveryError(
+                        "device login failed or no device code received; retry from the admin session"
+                    )
+                return

+    finally:
+        selector.close()
+        try:
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        except ProcessLookupError:
+            pass
+        proc.wait()
+

+"""Credential-free broker observations for announced deploy rolls."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import time
+
+
+def roll_status_payload(all_providers, cache, provider_states):
+    grants = {}
+    refresh_in_flight = cache.inflight_count() > 0
+    for name, provider in all_providers.items():
+        credentials = getattr(provider, "credentials", None)
+        stores = (
+            [(f"{name}:{c.credential_id}", c.auth_store) for c in credentials]
+            if credentials is not None
+            else [(name, getattr(provider, "auth_store", None))]
+        )
+        for key, store in stores:
+            grant = getattr(store, "grant_status", None)
+            if grant is not None:
+                grants[key] = dict(
+                    grant,
+                    provider=name,
+                    seconds_since_last_refresh=max(
+                        0,
+                        time.time()
+                        - (
+                            getattr(store, "last_refresh_completed_at", None)
+                            or grant["last_refresh"]
+                        ),
+                    ),
+                )
+        if not any(key == name or key.startswith(name + ":") for key in grants):
+            cached_grant = cache.cached_grant_status(name)
+            if cached_grant is not None and not name.startswith("github-app"):
+                grants[name] = dict(cached_grant, provider=name)
+        provider_refresh_in_flight = cache.refresh_in_flight(name) or any(
+            getattr(store, "refresh_in_flight", False) for _, store in stores
+        )
+        refresh_in_flight = refresh_in_flight or provider_refresh_in_flight
+        if name in provider_states:
+            provider_states[name]["refresh_in_flight"] = provider_refresh_in_flight
+
+    return {"grants": grants, "refresh_in_flight": refresh_in_flight}

+### Announced OAuth broker deploy rolls (ROLLGUARD-01)
+
+`main_catchup.broker_roll.roll()` owns the announced primary-only recreate used
+by the LiteLLM launcher's image-drift convergence and absent/unhealthy-primary
+repair. The executable entrypoint is:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m main_catchup.broker_roll --repo "$AGENT_OS_DEPLOY_CHECKOUT" \
+  --reason <image-drift|broker-repair> -- <primary-only recreate argv...>
+```
+
+The launcher supplies its process-group timeout wrapper (300 seconds plus a
+five-second kill grace); the entrypoint bounds the command to 310 seconds.
+The standby remains running. Before any recreate, the wrapper observes both
+brokers' `/readyz` provider states, grant refresh times/fingerprint prefixes,
+and refresh activity. It waits for no reported refresh in flight and at least
+120 seconds since the last refresh, bounded to 300 seconds by
+`BROKER_ROLL_WAIT_SECONDS`. Quiet-window exhaustion is recorded and proceeds
+only if the final snapshot proves the standby observable, serving at least one
+provider, and able to serve every provider served by either broker. Otherwise
+the roll is `deferred`, no command runs, and the primary stays untouched.
+A deferred invocation returns exit 75 but does not latch automatic suppression
+or send a critical roll page; a later invocation may retry after standby
+recovery. Persistent image drift retains the existing receipt and alarm path.
+
+Recognized transient launchd EIO, busy/I/O launch errors, and Docker daemon
+unavailability retry up to three total command attempts with one-second then
+two-second backoff. Permanent errors and timeouts do not retry, since a timeout
+may leave a partially completed recreate. Afterward, verification is bounded
+to 120 seconds by `BROKER_ROLL_VERIFY_SECONDS`, polling every two seconds with
+five-second status probe timeouts. Every previously serving provider must serve
+on both brokers afterward, and every previously observed per-broker grant's
+refresh time must remain equal or advance. An unobservable primary before a
+repair supplies no grant baseline; successful recovery is judged by its current
+observation and the providers observed serving on the standby. A current
+observation error, provider loss, grant regression, or terminal command error
+still fails verification. Legacy brokers without additive grant fields cannot
+prove continuity for those missing observations. Status-based quiet checks do
+not reserve a refresh lease: a refresh can start between the check and recreate.
+
+The mandatory owner-guarded, atomic history is
+`$HQ_ROOT/main-catchup/broker-roll.json`, mirrored best effort into
+`.state.json.brokerRoll`. Canonical HQ ownership is checked before directory
+creation; root writes preserve ownership and mode `0660`. History preparation
+failure returns exit 75 without recreating. The wrapper emits
+`main_catchup.broker_roll_started` / `main_catchup.broker_roll_finished` on the
+existing session-ledger worker-event surface with reason, merged PR numbers
+from `lastFFRange` (latest commit when absent/null), snapshots, outcome, wait
+and verification bounds, command attempts, differences, and an unavailability
+upper bound. Deferred records have zero command attempts and zero
+unavailability, with event status `warning`; verified events use `succeeded`.
+Git attribution reads are bounded to ten seconds; failures warn on stderr and
+continue with empty attribution so they do not prevent primary repair.
+
+Failed rolls page through the [shared alert delivery helper](../../scripts/alert-delivery.mjs) with critical priority
+and a roll-specific idempotency key. A persisted `failed` history suppresses
+later automatic recreates with exit 75 and retries undelivered pages. An
+operator must investigate the recorded difference and recover before removing
+that failed history to permit another automatic roll. A verified repair does
+not page or latch suppression. These outcomes do not gate the deploy
+fast-forward or other service convergence. `BROKER_ROLL_PRIMARY_URL` and
+`BROKER_ROLL_STANDBY_URL` override the default host probes at ports 4099 and
+4097; no config keys are added. `roll()` accepts injected observation, recreate,
+record, event, page, clock, and sleep seams for hermetic verification.

commit.message:
[codex] TGREACT-01: operator reactions and reply-to context are delivered to every agent in the channel (#8122)

## Summary

Telegram operator replies retain the target message and quote, and emoji additions/removals persist as shared chat context for every receiving agent. Residents, newly dispatched workers, worker follow-ups, receive, inbox_status and thread_history can see that context; reactions alone do not start work.



## What changed

Telegram webhook and polling ingest now accept message_reaction, authenticate the operator and store reaction changes without enqueueing a turn. Both allowed_updates lists include message_reaction. The additive schema.mjs migration (also invoked by the existing db/migrate.mjs entry point) creates operator_reactions without rewriting existing rows.

A shared operator-message-context helper resolves chat-scoped Telegram IDs to inbound, outbound or streamed-reply receipts, including receipts arriving after an event. Reply targets carry bounded excerpts and optional quotes. receive/inbox_status, thread_history, common resident injection, worker prompts and worker follow-ups expose human-content annotations separately from trusted provenance. The ATP runbook documents fields, context-only behavior, migration and activation. Fixture tests cover ingest, persistence, migration, additions/removals, deduplication, shared-chat visibility, unknown/outbound targets, receive/history and both resident harnesses.

No CI checks, workflow changes, ratchets, override labels or generated index edits were added.


## Why it matters

Requested by the operator in the ATP channel, inbound 174, on 2026-10-11 about 23:11Z after the Claude resident explained that inbound reactions were invisible:

> Ok we need to fix that. Can you launch a worker on that. Should be for all agents in the channel. Let's include specific message replies too if that is not included

This delivers the capability through common comms paths rather than a Claude-only fix. Reactions remain context-only to preserve zero idle turn cost, and excerpts/quotes/emoji never become trusted provenance. The resident's failed original dispatch is tracked separately as RESIDENTLEDGER-01 and is outside this change.


## Post-merge activities

Operator only; none of these actions were performed by this worker.

1. After main-catchup deploys this head, run `node modules/agent-gateway/db/migrate.mjs <comms-db-path>` from the deploy checkout as the comms DB owner, or let the owner's first initDb install the additive table. Existing messages remain readable.
2. Restart services retaining imported code through their documented owner/domain paths. For webhook ingress use `sudo ./scripts/os-restart.sh --restart inbound-receiver`. For standalone telegram-poller or integrated comms-runner, inspect the rendered tracked plist Label and actual domain, then use `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/<rendered-label>` for system installs or `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<owner-uid>/<rendered-label>` from the owner account for GUI installs. Restart attached comms MCP readers and resident drainers through their existing registry paths. Restart only the configured ingress mode; do not create competing pollers.
3. In webhook mode, re-register with the existing managed `modules/agent-gateway/scripts/setup-webhooks.mjs` under its documented secret environment and verify getWebhookInfo.allowed_updates contains message_reaction. In polling mode, the restarted poller requests message_reaction in getUpdates.allowed_updates automatically.
4. Make each receiving bot an administrator in the operator's group/supergroup. Telegram requires administrator rights and explicit message_reaction subscription, and does not send bot-set reactions (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update). Private-chat availability is limited by that provider contract; anonymous aggregate updates cannot authenticate the operator and are intentionally excluded.

GitHub CI and AMA must be green before merge. The managed local publication gate is budget-deferred after its automatic retry; no override was used.

## Ticket
TGREACT-01

## Spec
none

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

364 scoped Node tests passed across operator-message-context, webhook registration, Telegram poller, resident inbound, thread_history, drainer inbound, operator dispatch and comms tools; 11 scoped pytest resident-transcript-adapter tests passed. After the worker-prompt/follow-up addition, the 227 relevant Node tests were rerun and all passed. Changed MJS files passed node --check; both changed Python files passed Ruff lint/format; docs linkcheck and git diff --check passed. Validation used temporary fixture databases, fixture Telegram payloads and mocked API functions, with unstubbed fetch blocked in the comprehensive run.

The first managed push rejected a module-relative runbook script link; it was corrected and linkcheck passed. The final normal git-safe push succeeded with managed budget-deferred evidence after two budget overruns comparing baseline. No live host service was changed or restarted, and no message/reaction was sent to a real chat.

## Out-of-scope changes

(none)

The operator asked the Claude resident over Telegram to launch a fix worker (inbound id 174, about 23:11). The
resident ran, from its own shell:

`hq dispatch --project agent-talk-protocol --parent-session lrq:lrq_0ade1ee4-... --worker-class claude-code --repo
laceyenterprises/agent-os --ticket ATP-comms-inbound-reactions-replies --task-kind coding --completion-shape pr
--idempotency-key atp-inbound-174-... --await-accepted --prompt <file>`

- The command printed `dispatch.stage_timings` with `"insert": 31.9` and a launch id,
  `lrq_ca63ee28-7fd3-4d47-839c-4beae80f8c1a` (run `wrun_3375258e-...`), then
  `[hq] boot-stage optional-overlays-skipped emit failed (non-fatal)`, and then waited. After 6 minutes 53 seconds
  it was still waiting (process asleep, one unreaped child, no database connection open) and the SRE session ended
  it.
- That launch id does not exist in the fleet ledger: no row in `launch_requests` or `worker_runs` of
  `agent_os_ledger`, and no dispatch directory.
- The environment of that command (names and database names only):
  `AGENT_OS_SESSION_LEDGER_DSN=postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/vdb_test_3dcbd9ece13e3173_30aad641`,
  `AGENT_OS_WORKER_VDB_MODE=clone`, `AGENT_OS_WORKER_VDB_OWNER=worker:resident-claude-responder`,
  `AGENT_OS_SESSION_LEDGER_CANONICAL_DSN=postgresql://...@127.0.0.1:6432/agent_os_ledger`.
  So the launch request was inserted into the resident's disposable test copy of the ledger, which no dispatch
  daemon reads.
- The resident then told the operator the worker had been launched. It had not. The SRE session dispatched the

commit.message:
[codex] DISKLEAK-10: the workspace cleanup survives a read-only directory, keeps pace with new workers, and measures the tree without a full du (#8128)

## Summary

A read-only or user-immutable leftover no longer wedges worker cleanup. Completed passes exit successfully while naming individual worker failures, metadata reduction has an independent quarter-hour cadence, and disk growth comes from incremental workspace measurements.



## What changed

The canonical teardown and metadata retention paths repair permissions only on owned inodes, clear UF_IMMUTABLE through descriptor-based traversal, avoid following symlinks, retry removal, and retain existing Git/PR, salvage, gym grading, dirty-workspace, and age protections. The shell drain rotates a persisted cursor and places previously failed workers after other candidates. Metadata sweeps inspect up to 1,000 slots with a 600-second budget every 900 seconds on a separate single-flight thread and ledger connection, independently of archive retention. Cached/local-only candidates precede slow PR lookups; canonical teardowns share the existing complete, TTL-bounded per-repository open-PR snapshot cache rather than treating a latest closed PR as proof that no PR is open. [codex] CODEXRELOGIN-01: `hq broker relogin codex` runs the whole recovery and sends the operator the device code (#8129)

## Summary

Adds an attended, end-to-end Codex recovery command that prints and pages the device link/code, then publishes and verifies the recovered grant through the fleet. The operator only needs to approve the device code.



## What changed

Adds oauth_broker.relogin and hq broker relogin codex [--check-only]. Recovery backs up admin credentials, uses bounded device login and the existing Sentinel page channel, loads/kicks the root mirror, waits for file agreement and both brokers' Codex can_serve, syncs as runtime owner, compares worker/broker access hashes and runs an ephemeral smoke. Noninteractive sudo identifies unavailable user switching without prompting. Updates RUNBOOK-broker-ops.md and permanent-refresh failure pages; adds fake-binary recovery tests and page-text regression coverage. No CI checks, gates, config keys or workflows added.

Claude-code follow-up would need bridge-owner login (rather than Codex device auth), the Claude keychain/bridge publication path, Claude-specific credential inspection and worker token consumption, plus Claude broker readiness and smoke verification. This PR implements only Codex.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 left Codex unavailable for 69 minutes and recovery required rediscovering the credential publication and worker-sync sequence. Builds on PR 8106, PR 8108 and PR 8109. Operator: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". When recovery initially waited for intervention, the operator said: "You have the tools you don't need operator intervention. It has been done before." This command starts recovery and delivers the approval request directly, while keeping upstream refresh tokens out of worker files and out of output.


## Post-merge activities

Normal main-catchup deployment makes the hq command available. Deploy the updated watchdog through its documented operator restart path so future permanent-refresh pages name the recovery command. No live recovery or restarts were performed by this worker.

## Ticket
CODEXRELOGIN-01

## Spec
none

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

22 scoped tests passed: 17 isolated recovery tests, four selected permanent-refresh page regressions and CLI reference parity. Stand-in Codex/launchctl/pager/sync binaries and temporary fake auth/log files verify order, repeatability, failure stops, timeout handling, noninteractive user switching, no-op check-only, token redaction and safe mirror-direction reporting; stand-in HTTP broker covers serving Codex despite aggregate HTTP 503. Ruff check/format, git diff --check and shellcheck gate passed. Initial managed push correctly rejected stale CLI reference; regenerated the reference and its parity test passes. No full worker-pool suite or live auth/page/service operations. Managed exact-head push succeeded with budget-deferred attestation after its two automatic budget overruns; GitHub CI and AMA must be green before merge.

## Out-of-scope changes

(none)

[codex] ROLLGUARD-01: a broker roll is announced, waits out a refresh, and is verified provider by provider (#8130)

## Summary

Deploy broker recreates now record both brokers before and after, wait for observed refresh activity to settle, announce the roll on the existing ledger event surface, and verify serving providers and grant times. A failed verification pages with the exact difference, preserves the standby, and suppresses subsequent automatic recreates.



## What changed

Main-catchup owns the roll wrapper and deploy record, with a 300-second quiet-window wait budget and a 120-second post-command verification budget; individual status probes are bounded to five seconds. Both launcher recreate paths use it. Image-drift convergence recreates only the primary, leaving the standby running. Additive broker /readyz fields expose per-grant refresh time and hash prefix, refresh ages, and in-flight refresh observations including direct credential leases. The session-ledger event allowlist registers the two announcements using existing phases and statuses. Image equality repairs the persisted drift receipt. No config.yaml keys, CI checks, ratchets, override labels, or new fail-closed auth conditions were added.

Limits: timing uses status observations; a refresh can start between the last observation and recreate, so this is not an atomic refresh reservation. The reported unavailability duration is explicitly an upper bound from recreate start to verification. A pre-upgrade broker has no grant-status fields: its initial empty grant snapshot cannot prove grant continuity, and the native standby must load the additive status code before subsequent rolls have complete grant evidence on both instances. These limitations are recorded in the walkthrough rather than presented as stronger guarantees.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 showed that a silent deploy could load a rolled-back grant while workers were in flight. Operator, verbatim: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". This complements PR 8106 (grant-aware mirror), PR 8108 (broker grant monotonicity), and PR 8109 (auth paging and builder holds), with deploy evidence and provider-by-provider outcome verification. The existing grant store remains the protection against an actual rollback; this change makes the deployment and any observed regression visible.


## Post-merge activities

The deploy of this pull request rolls the broker. Normal main-catchup propagation activates the wrapper and primary status fields; use the normal operator-managed standby activation path for its additive status fields, while preserving standby service during primary rolls. No config migration is needed. After a failed verification, investigate and recover the exact provider/grant difference before removing the failed roll record to re-enable automatic rolls. No live host actions were performed by this worker.

## Ticket
ROLLGUARD-01

## Spec
none

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

14 scoped main-catchup tests passed (roll and image drift); 76 broker auth-file/token-cache unit tests passed in the declared test environment; one fake-provider /readyz integration test passed (47 unrelated endpoint tests deselected). Launcher and broker-image-drift shell tests returned zero; the existing completion guard records its known CLZ-01 skip for the launcher suite tail. Ruff lint/format, shellcheck gate, docs linkcheck and git diff --check passed. Tests used temporary directories, fake credentials/providers, and stubbed alert seams. Managed git-safe push accepted the final head as budget-deferred after its built-in retry; GitHub CI and AMA still gate merge.

## Out-of-scope changes

(none)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared, opt-in prompt refusal for the reached installer chain.
+installer_unattended_init() {
+  case "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" in
+    0) return 0 ;;
+    1) ;;
+    *) printf 'unattended-input: AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE must be 0 or 1\n' >&2; return 64 ;;
+  esac
+  set +x +v
+  export AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 CI=1 GH_ASSUME_YES=1
+  export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  export SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  # Ignore a supplied interactive SSH command: unattended cannot inherit an agent
+  # or password prompt. Host verification remains enabled.
+  export GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oIdentityAgent=none -oBatchMode=yes -oConnectTimeout=15 -oServerAliveInterval=15 -oServerAliveCountMax=3'
+  export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1
+  exec </dev/null
+}
+
+installer_unattended_sudo_check() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  [[ "$(id -u)" == 0 ]] && return 0
+  command sudo -n true || {
+    printf 'unattended-input: pre-authorized noninteractive sudo required\n' >&2
+    return 77
+  }
+}
+
+# Functions preserve attended argv exactly. Export only in unattended mode so
+# reached Bash helpers also refuse askpass. sudo policies still authorize every
+# operation; a cached timestamp is never treated as an enduring grant.
+installer_unattended_functions() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  sudo() {
+    local arg args=()
+    for arg in "$@"; do
+      [[ "$arg" == -A ]] || args+=("$arg")
+    done
+    command sudo -n --preserve-env=AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE,GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT,GIT_ASKPASS,SSH_ASKPASS,GIT_SSH_COMMAND,GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME,GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL,GIT_COMMITTER_NAME,GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL,SUDO_ASKPASS "${args[@]}"
+  }
+  git() {
+    local identity=()
+    if [[ -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" && -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+      identity=(-c "user.name=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" -c "user.email=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL")
+    fi
+    command git "${identity[@]}" -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=/usr/bin/false \
+      -c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0 -c fetch.writeCommitGraph=false "$@"
+  }
+  export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'credential.helper=' 'core.askPass=/usr/bin/false' 'maintenance.auto=false' 'gc.auto=0' 'fetch.writeCommitGraph=false'"
+  export -f sudo git
+}
+
+installer_unattended_core_inputs() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: acknowledge unsupported OAuth/Keychain with AGENT_OS_UNATTENDED_EXCLUDE_KEYCHAIN=1\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  if [[ -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+    printf 'unattended-input: explicit AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME and AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL required\n' >&2
+    return 64
+  fi
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME"
+  export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL"
+}
+
+# Only idempotent provisioning operations belong here. Unknown and structural
+# failures stop immediately; a transient signature never overrides an auth,
+# permission, certificate-verification or configuration error in the same run.
+installer_output_is_transient() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if grep -Eiq 'permission denied|operation not permitted|authentication failed|could not read (username|password)|repository .*not found|repository not found|host key verification failed|certificate verify failed|certificate verification failed|unable to get local issuer certificate|self.signed certificate|invalid (argument|configuration|plist)|no such file or directory|EACCES|EPERM|E401|E403' "$@"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$kind" == runtime ]] && grep -Eiq 'bootstrap failed: 5: input/output error|(^|[^[:alnum:]_])EIO([^[:alnum:]_]|$)|resource temporarily unavailable|service not yet bootstrapped' "$@"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  grep -Eiq 'timed out|timeout|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|EAI_AGAIN|connection reset|connection refused|temporary failure in name resolution|could not resolve host|could not resolve hostname|TLS handshake|SSL.*(connect|handshake)|early EOF|remote end hung up unexpectedly|HTTP[^[:digit:]]+50[234]|(error|response|returned)[^[:digit:]]+50[234]' "$@"
+}
+
+installer_run_with_retry() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  local capture_dir attempt status delay
+  capture_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return 1
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    status=0
+    "$@" >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" || status=$?
+    cat "$capture_dir/stdout"
+    cat "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2
+    if [[ "$status" == 0 ]]; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! installer_output_is_transient "$kind" "$capture_dir/stdout" "$capture_dir/stderr"; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return "$status"
+    fi
+    # Fixed provisioning policy, matching the launchd post-bootout recovery
+    # window. No exponential arithmetic or retry tuning inputs to duplicate.
+    case "$attempt" in 1) delay=2 ;; 2) delay=5 ;; esac
+    printf 'unattended-retry: %s transient failure on attempt %s/3; retrying in %ss\n' "$kind" "$attempt" "$delay" >&2
+    sleep "$delay"
+  done
+}
+
+# Existing producer + TIH-01 strict adapter, before launchd mutations. No auth
+# probe is executed on the builder host; callers run this only in the lab install.
+installer_unattended_precheck() {
+  local repo_root="$1" stage="$2" timeout_seconds="${3:-120}"
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  python3 - "$repo_root" "$stage" "$timeout_seconds" <<'PYCODE'
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+stage = sys.argv[2]
+try:
+    timeout_seconds = float(sys.argv[3])
+    if not 0 < timeout_seconds <= 120:
+        raise ValueError
+except ValueError:
+    print("unattended-input: precheck timeout must be positive and at most 120 seconds", file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(64)
+sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "modules/test-install-host"))
+from checks import adapt
+from contracts import Stage
+
+
+def preserve_stderr(diagnostics):
+    # Raw producer output can include auth identity. Keep it out of the public
+    # installer log, but leave a mode-0600 file for the invoking operator.
+    if diagnostics:
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
+            mode="w", prefix="agent-os-precheck-", suffix=".stderr", delete=False
+        ) as diagnostic_file:
+            diagnostic_file.write(diagnostics)
+        print(f"unattended-input: precheck stderr saved to {diagnostic_file.name}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+process = subprocess.Popen(
+    ["bash", str(root / "scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh"), "--json"],
+    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, start_new_session=True,
+)
+try:
+    raw, diagnostics = process.communicate(timeout=timeout_seconds)
+except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+    _, diagnostics = process.communicate()
+    preserve_stderr(diagnostics)
+    print("unattended-input: precheck timed out", file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(124)
+coverage = adapt("precheck", raw, stage=Stage(stage),
+                 boot_id="installer-precheck", exit_code=process.returncode)
+if not coverage.qualified:
+    preserve_stderr(diagnostics)
+# Normalized reasons contain check IDs only; raw identity/auth messages are not
+# forwarded into the installer log. Actual boot provenance belongs to TIH-05.
+print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "qualified": coverage.qualified,
+                  "reasons": coverage.reasons}))
+sys.exit(0 if coverage.qualified else 1)
+PYCODE
+}
+
+installer_brew_bundle() {
+  local brew_bin="$1" brewfile="$2" temporary_file status
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$brewfile" --no-lock
+    return
+  fi
+  temporary_file="$(mktemp)" || return 1
+  # Preserve the canonical formula inventory and CLI casks only.
+  awk '$1 != "cask" || $2 == "\"1password-cli\"" || $2 == "\"claude-code\"" || $2 == "\"codex\"" { print }' \
+    "$brewfile" >"$temporary_file" || { rm -f "$temporary_file"; return 1; }
+  printf 'brew "colima"\nbrew "docker"\nbrew "docker-compose"\n' >>"$temporary_file"
+  status=0
+  installer_run_with_retry network "$brew_bin" bundle --file="$temporary_file" --no-lock || status=$?
+  rm -f "$temporary_file"
+  [[ "$status" == 0 ]] || {
+    printf 'dependency provisioning failed; refusing partial install\n' >&2
+    return "$status"
+  }
+  printf 'coverage-excluded: protected GUI casks (LuLu/TCC, Docker Desktop, desktop applications)\n' >&2
+}

+## Operator reactions and reply context (TGREACT-01)
+
+Telegram messages now carry `reply_to` with `telegram_message_id`, known
+`inbound_id` or `outbound_id`, a bounded `excerpt`, and optional `quote` (text,
+position and is_manual). Unknown/deleted targets keep their Telegram ID and
+excerpt; later history reads resolve targets when their receipt arrives.
+Existing rows remain readable. `initDb`/`db/migrate.mjs` installs the additive
+`operator_reactions` table without rewriting historical messages.
+
+Authenticated operator `message_reaction` updates persist old/new reaction
+sets, actor ID and Telegram timestamp. `reactions` on a message lists changes
+(`added`, `removed`, `current`); `reaction_context` on `receive`, `inbox_status`
+and `thread_history` includes the latest 50 chat events, including unknown
+message targets. These are shared by agents receiving in the same chat, even
+when another agent's bot ingested the event. Other chats stay scoped out.
+Receive annotations and the common resident injection include reply context
+and recent reactions. Worker operator prompts and follow-up injections include both contexts too.
+Only IDs are references: excerpts, quotes and reaction values remain labelled
+`human_message_not_provenance`, never trusted attribution or instructions.
+
+Reactions are **context only**: they do not enqueue inbound work, send typing
+acknowledgments, invoke commands or wake residents/workers. A subsequent
+operator message or explicit comms read exposes them, including removals.
+Anonymous/chat-actor reactions cannot authenticate as the operator and are
+ignored; bot reactions and aggregate `message_reaction_count` are not ingested.
+
+Post-merge activities (operator only):
+
+1. Let main-catchup deploy, then use the registered service owner and restart
+   path in `scripts/os-restart.sh` for the inbound receiver
+   (`sudo ./scripts/os-restart.sh --restart inbound-receiver`). For standalone
+   `telegram-poller` or integrated `comms-runner`, inspect the rendered tracked
+   plist's Label and actual launchd domain, then use
+   `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/<rendered-label>` for system installs,
+   or `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<owner-uid>/<rendered-label>` from the owner
+   account for GUI installs. Restart the configured ingress mode only, plus
+   attached comms readers/drainers that retain imported code. The additive migration runs on comms DB init;
+   alternatively run `node modules/agent-gateway/db/migrate.mjs <comms-db>` as
+   the comms DB owner before restarting readers.
+2. In webhook mode, run the existing managed `modules/agent-gateway/scripts/setup-webhooks.mjs`
+   registration under its documented secret environment. Verify
+   `getWebhookInfo.allowed_updates` includes `message_reaction`; in polling
+   mode the restarted poller requests it in `getUpdates.allowed_updates`.
+3. For the operator's group/supergroup, make each receiving bot an
+   administrator. Telegram requires administrator rights and explicit
+   `message_reaction` subscription, and does not deliver bot-set reactions
+   ([Telegram Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update)). Private

+`retention/worker-disk-trend.json` is an incremental allocated-byte cache,
+serialized by `retention/worker-disk-trend.lock` and atomically replaced by
+`worker_disk_trend.py`. Its fields are:
+
+| Field | Shape / meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `time`, `bytes` | Unix sample time and sum of last successful allocated bytes for present worker slots. Teardown updates `bytes` without advancing the sample time. |
+| `sample` | `{time, bytes}` from the last completed apply measurement; growth compares this pair, not teardown's updated aggregate. Absent before the first completed measurement. |
+| `entries` | Dictionary keyed by worker ID. Each item may contain numeric `bytes`, `measuredAt` and `attemptedAt` Unix seconds, and string `error`. Failures keep prior bytes/time; never-measured slots omit them. Removed slots are pruned. |
+| `measurementFailures` | Array of `{worker, reason}` strings. Teardown keeps the latest 50 failed measurements even if a later measurement succeeds. Apply returns pending events plus current entry errors, then clears pending events; dry-run leaves them intact. |
+
+Completed apply passes persist the cache even under pressure; dry-run never
+persists. Measurement rotates by `attemptedAt`, refreshes successful entries
+older than 900 seconds, and uses a 15-second pass budget with at most two seconds
+per tree. Budget-deferred entries carry an explicit error. Teardown records
+before/after with a five-second measurement deadline. `diskTrend` reports
+`workers_gib`, nullable `workers_growth_gib_per_hour`, `measurementFailures`,
+`unmeasured` (entries without bytes), and `status` (`measured` or `partial`). A
+store/traversal failure can instead return `status: failed` and `reason`. Cached
+bytes with failed refreshes are partial coverage, not a fresh complete census.
+The first sample has a null growth rate. Legacy `{time, bytes}` files remain
+readable, but only the new `sample` pair supplies the previous rate baseline.

+### Telegram human reply and reaction context
+
+`lib/operator-message-context.mjs` keeps Telegram reply quotes and operator
+reactions as human conversation annotations, labelled
+`human_message_not_provenance`. Inbound `reply_to` contains the target's
+`telegram_message_id`, a text/caption `excerpt` bounded to 512 Unicode code
+points, and optional `quote` (`text` bounded to 512 code points, `position`,
+`is_manual`). Target resolution uses the chat and Telegram message id across
+bots, adding `inbound_id`, `outbound_id`, or `journal_id` when a local receipt is
+known. Unknown targets remain visible and are resolved again on later reads.
+Target lookups use indexed generated Telegram IDs in `inbound_queue` and
+`outbox_items`, plus a confirmed-delivery journal index. `initDb()` adds the
+virtual columns to existing databases and builds indexes once; generated IDs
+follow later payload/receipt updates automatically. Invalid historical JSON
+produces no message ID; inbound chat IDs fall back to `sender_id`.
+Agent chat discovery seeks successive chat IDs in the `(agent_id,
+telegram_chat_id)` index, so polling work scales with distinct chats rather
+than historical inbound rows.
+
+Webhook setup (`scripts/setup-webhooks.mjs`) registers and verifies
+`allowed_updates` containing `message`, `callback_query`, `edited_message`, and
+`message_reaction`; the long-poller requests the same set. In either ingress
+mode, user-backed reaction updates pass the ingress/sender/operator-chat gates
+before insertion into `operator_reactions`. Anonymous `actor_chat` and aggregate
+`message_reaction_count` updates are unsupported. Retries and copies received by
+different bots deduplicate on the stored event tuple. Reaction-only updates do
+not enqueue messages, dispatch workers, inject resident turns, or send replies.
+
+Comms MCP exposes the annotations on its read surfaces:
+
+- `receive` messages carry optional `reply_to` and per-message `reactions`; its
+  top-level `reaction_context` includes the newest 50 events across chats found
+  in the agent's Telegram inbound rows, sorted globally newest first. Shared
+  context is read once at the response root, never repeated in each message. Context
+  remains available even when the pending queue is empty.
+- `inbox_status` returns the same top-level `reaction_context` alongside the
+  pending count.
+- `thread_history` preserves its authenticated own-thread scope and returns
+  inbound `reply_to`, per-message `reactions`, and up to 50 recent chat events
+  in top-level `reaction_context`. The existing byte cap applies to annotations
+  too; `reactions_truncated` reports when recent events were dropped to fit.
+
+Each reaction records actor, timestamp, target message id, added/removed/current
+emoji or custom emoji, and any resolved local target. Drainer claims and
+responder prompts also include this bounded context with explicit human-content
+labels. A drainer claim reads per-message annotations and its shared chat context
+once after the queue lease transaction commits, keeping context reads outside
+the write lock. Quotes and emoji do not change policy, trusted attribution, completion
+state, or wake behavior.

+            ("operation now in progress", "cannot connect to the docker daemon"),
+            (r"bootstrap failed: 5\b",),
+        )
+    return isinstance(exc, OSError) and exc.errno in {errno.EIO, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EBUSY}
+
+
+def _recreate(command):
+    # Keep command diagnostics without a pipe that can hide successful progress.
+    with tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+", encoding="utf-8") as stderr:
+        try:
+            return subprocess.run(command, check=True, timeout=310, stderr=stderr, text=True)
+        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            exc.stderr = stderr.read()
+            raise
+        finally:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            sys.stderr.write(stderr.read())
+            sys.stderr.flush()
+
+
+def snapshot(url):
+    try:
+        response = urllib.request.urlopen(url + "/readyz", timeout=5)
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+        response = exc  # A 503 still carries provider and grant evidence.
+    with response:
+        body = json.load(response)
+    return {
+        "provider_states": body.get("provider_states", {}),
+        "grants": body.get("grants", {}),
+        "refresh_in_flight": body.get("refresh_in_flight", False),
+    }
+
+
+def _serving_providers(states):
+    return {
+        provider
+        for body in states.values()
+        for provider, state in body.get("provider_states", {}).items()
+        if state.get("can_serve")
+    }
+
+
+def _standby_preflight(states):
+    standby = states.get("standby", {})
+    if not standby or standby.get("observationError"):
+        return ["standby: status observation unavailable"]
+    if not _serving_providers({"standby": standby}):
+        return ["standby: no serving providers observed"]
+    return [
+        f"standby provider {provider}: cannot cover primary during recreate"
+        for provider in sorted(_serving_providers(states))
+        if not standby.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve")
+    ]
+
+
+def differences(before, after):
+    result = []
+    serving = _serving_providers(before)
+    for broker, previous in before.items():
+        current = after.get(broker, {})
+        if current.get("observationError"):
+            result.append(f"{broker}: status observation unavailable")
+            continue
+        for provider in serving:
+            if not current.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve"):
+                result.append(f"{broker} provider {provider}: can_serve true -> false/missing")
+        for grant, state in previous.get("grants", {}).items():
+            new = current.get("grants", {}).get(grant, {})
+            if new.get("last_refresh", -1) < state["last_refresh"]:
+                result.append(
+                    f"{broker} grant {grant}: last_refresh {state['last_refresh']} -> {new.get('last_refresh', 'missing')}"
+                )
+    return result
+
+
+def quiet(states):
+    if any(body.get("refresh_in_flight") for body in states.values()):
+        return False
+    if any(
+        grant.get("seconds_since_last_refresh", QUIET_SECONDS) < QUIET_SECONDS
+        for body in states.values()
+        for grant in body.get("grants", {}).values()
+    ):
+        return False
+    return all(
+        not state.get("refresh_in_flight")
+        and (
+            state.get("refresh_age_measured_from") != "last_refresh"
+            or state.get("seconds_since_last_refresh", 0) >= QUIET_SECONDS
+        )
+        for body in states.values()
+        for state in body.get("provider_states", {}).values()
+    )
+
+
+def roll(
+    *,
+    read,
+    recreate,
+    record,
+    emit,
+    page,
+    reason,
+    prs,
+    clock=time.monotonic,
+    sleep=time.sleep,
+    wait_seconds=WAIT_SECONDS,
+    verify_seconds=VERIFY_SECONDS,
+):
+    start = clock()
+    before = read()
+    while not quiet(before) and clock() - start < wait_seconds:
+        sleep(min(POLL_SECONDS, max(0, wait_seconds - (clock() - start))))
+        before = read()
+    evidence = {
+        "rollId": uuid.uuid4().hex,
+        "reason": reason,
+        "prs": prs,
+        "before": before,
+        "waitSeconds": clock() - start,
+        "waitBoundSeconds": wait_seconds,
+        "waitBoundReached": not quiet(before),
+        "verifyBoundSeconds": verify_seconds,
+    }
+
+    def announce(kind):
+        try:
+            emit(kind, evidence)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence.setdefault("eventErrors", []).append(type(exc).__name__)
+
+    record(evidence)
+    announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_started")
+    preflight = _standby_preflight(before)
+    if preflight:
+        # No command ran: retain the primary and allow a later health-based retry.
+        evidence.update(
+            after=before,
+            differences=preflight,
+            commandAttempts=0,
+            commandError=None,
+            result="deferred",
+            unavailabilitySeconds=0,
+            unavailabilityMeasurement="no recreate attempted",
+        )
+        record(evidence)
+        announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_finished")
+        record(evidence)
+        return evidence
+    unavailable = clock()
+    error = None
+    for attempt in range(COMMAND_ATTEMPTS):
+        evidence["commandAttempts"] = attempt + 1
+        try:
+            recreate()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            # Timeouts can leave a partially completed recreate: do not replay them.
+            if not _transient_command_error(exc) or attempt == COMMAND_ATTEMPTS - 1:
+                error = type(exc).__name__
+                break
+            sleep(bounded_exponential_delay(attempt, base_seconds=1, max_seconds=2))
+        else:
+            break
+    deadline = clock() + verify_seconds
+    after = read()
+    delta = differences(before, after)
+    while delta and clock() < deadline:
+        sleep(min(POLL_SECONDS, max(0, deadline - clock())))
+        after = read()
+        delta = differences(before, after)
+    evidence.update(
+        after=after,
+        differences=delta,
+        commandError=error,
+        result="failed" if delta or error else "verified",
+        unavailabilitySeconds=clock() - unavailable,
+        unavailabilityMeasurement="upper bound from recreate start to verified status",
+    )
+    record(evidence)
+    announce("main_catchup.broker_roll_finished")
+    record(evidence)
+    if delta or error:
+        try:
+            evidence["pageDelivered"] = bool(page(evidence))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence["pageDelivered"] = False
+            evidence["pageError"] = type(exc).__name__
+        record(evidence)
+    return evidence
+
+
+def event_status(evidence):
+    result = evidence.get("result", "running")
+    return {"verified": "succeeded", "deferred": "warning"}.get(result, result)
+
+
+def _number(name, default):
+    try:
+        value = float(os.environ.get(name, default))
+        return value if math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0 else default
+    except ValueError:
+        return default
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--reason", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("command", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    from agent_os_config.roots import hq_root_preferring_legacy_env
+    from main_catchup import stateio
+    from main_catchup.broker_image_drift import _write_state
+    from main_catchup.broker_image_drift import _prepare_state_parent
+
+    root = Path(hq_root_preferring_legacy_env())
+    history = root / "main-catchup/broker-roll.json"
+    try:
+        _prepare_state_parent(history, owner_root=root)
+    except OSError:
+        return 75  # Never recreate when the durable failure guard cannot be owned safely.
+    # Failed verification suppresses automatic repeats across launcher processes.
+    try:
+        prior = json.loads(history.read_text())
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        prior = {}
+    urls = {
+        "primary": os.environ.get("BROKER_ROLL_PRIMARY_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4099"),
+        "standby": os.environ.get("BROKER_ROLL_STANDBY_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4097"),
+    }
+
+    def read():
+        result = {}
+        for name, url in urls.items():
+            try:
+                result[name] = snapshot(url)
+            except (OSError, ValueError):
+                result[name] = {"provider_states": {}, "grants": {}, "observationError": True}
+        return result
+
+    def record(evidence):
+        # The suppression record is mandatory; do not roll without durable evidence.
+        _write_state(history, evidence, owner_root=root)
+        try:
+            # stateio locks as the directory owner and preserves HQ ownership for root.
+            stateio._write_state(root, brokerRoll=evidence)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            evidence.setdefault("recordErrors", []).append(type(exc).__name__)
+
+    def emit(kind, evidence):
+        from main_catchup.daemon import _append_audit_event
+        from session_ledger.db import LedgerDatabase
+        from session_ledger.db_path import resolve_ledger_target
+
+        target = resolve_ledger_target(hq_root=root, module_anchor=args.repo)
+        db = LedgerDatabase(target.db_path)
+        try:
+            _append_audit_event(
+                db,
+                args.repo,
+                kind,
+                summary=args.reason,
+                payload=evidence,
+                status=event_status(evidence),
+                phase="operating",
+            )
+        finally:
+            db.close()
+
+    def page(evidence):
+        # Same auth page delivery helper as PR 8109; keep the deploy wrapper
+        # independent of the broker's aiohttp/metrics runtime dependencies.
+        subprocess.run(
+            [
+                os.environ.get("SENTINEL_NODE_BIN", "node"),
+                str(args.repo / "scripts/alert-delivery.mjs"),
+                "--message",
+                "OAuth broker deploy roll failed: "
+                + "; ".join(evidence["differences"] or [evidence["commandError"]]),
+                "--source",
+                "oauth-broker",
+                "--idempotency-key",
+                "oauth-broker:auth:roll:" + evidence["rollId"],
+                "--metadata-json",
+                json.dumps(
+                    {"alertKey": "broker:auth:roll", "priority": "critical", "roll": evidence}
+                ),
+                "--rate-limit-seconds",
+                "900",
+            ],
+            check=True,
+            timeout=20,
+            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        )
+        return True
+
+    if prior.get("result") == "failed":
+        if not prior.get("pageDelivered"):
+            try:
+                prior["pageDelivered"] = bool(page(prior))
+            except Exception as exc:
+                prior["pageError"] = type(exc).__name__
+            record(prior)
+        return 75
+
+    command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == ["--"] else args.command
+    deploy_range = stateio._read_state(root).get("lastFFRange") or {}
+    revisions = (
+        [f"{deploy_range['fromSha']}..{deploy_range['toSha']}"]
+        if deploy_range.get("fromSha") and deploy_range.get("toSha")
+        else ["-1"]
+    )
+    try:
+        subjects = subprocess.run(
+            [
+                "git",
+                "-C",
+                str(args.repo),
+                "log",
+                *revisions,
+                "--format=%s",
+                "--",
+                "platform/oauth-broker",
+                "modules/model-routing-budget-control/runtime",
+            ],
+            check=True,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=10,
+        ).stdout
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+        print(
+            f"broker-roll: merged PR attribution unavailable ({type(exc).__name__})",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        subjects = ""
+    prs = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\(#(\d+)\)", subjects)))
+    result = roll(
+        read=read,
+        recreate=lambda: _recreate(command),
+        record=record,
+        emit=emit,
+        page=page,
+        reason=args.reason,
+        prs=prs,
+        wait_seconds=_number("BROKER_ROLL_WAIT_SECONDS", WAIT_SECONDS),
+        verify_seconds=_number("BROKER_ROLL_VERIFY_SECONDS", VERIFY_SECONDS),
+    )
+    return 0 if result["result"] == "verified" else 75
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
